comments.body:
🤖 GRUG-XEM-008 result: material direct shared-bank conflict appears only at the midpoint

This read-only d512 diagnostic tests whether layers 2 and 3 persistently request opposing updates from the one expert bank they share after checkpoint conversion. The Stage-B start is the selected Stage-A endpoint: a frozen-router, bank-only checkpoint after 50,069,504 Stage-A local-recovery tokens. `S′` is its matched bank-only Stage-B continuation, which keeps routers and QB state frozen and trains the same bank with CE `1.0`, teacher-logit KL `0.1`, and routed-MoE loss `1.0`; its midpoint and endpoint are 25,034,752 and 50,069,504 Stage-B continuation tokens.

At each checkpoint, the diagnostic uses the same 16 unseen continuation batches, loader indices 382 through 397. It computes separate layer-2 and layer-3 gradients of normalized teacher-on-student-state routed-MoE error with respect to the shared bank. The primary aggregate cosine is between the two 16-batch mean gradient trees. A checkpoint passes only if aggregate cosine is at most `-0.10`, the batch-mean bootstrap interval has an upper bound below zero, at least 12 of 16 batch cosines are negative, cancellation is at least `0.10`, and the smaller/larger gradient-norm ratio is at least `0.25`. Persistent material conflict requires at least two of three checkpoints to pass.

| Checkpoint | Aggregate cosine | Cancellation | Norm ratio | Batch mean cosine (95% bootstrap interval) | Negative batches | Gate |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---|
| Stage-B start (selected Stage-A endpoint), 0 Stage-B tokens | -0.045448 | 0.146092 | 0.180523 | -0.151560 [-0.185357, -0.112829] | 14/16 | Fail |
| `S′` midpoint, 25,034,752 tokens | -0.104190 | 0.329587 | 0.899402 | -0.064347 [-0.076626, -0.050098] | 16/16 | Pass |
| `S′` endpoint, 50,069,504 tokens | -0.017830 | 0.161887 | 0.216225 | -0.066230 [-0.079956, -0.050099] | 14/16 | Fail |

Projection entries below are `cosine / norm ratio` for the gate, up, and down expert matrices. For per-expert dots `d_e = g_{2,e} · g_{3,e}`, negative-dot energy share is `sum_e max(-d_e, 0) / sum_e abs(d_e)`. Expert counts and energy shares are descriptive components, not statistical replicates.

| Checkpoint | Gate | Up | Down | Negative expert dots | Negative-dot energy share |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Stage-B start | -0.040544 / 0.148713 | -0.038550 / 0.149368 | -0.074415 / 0.321547 | 254/256 | 0.894903 |
| `S′` midpoint | -0.087410 / 0.993027 | -0.079980 / 0.979890 | -0.147733 / 0.738705 | 234/256 | 0.922178 |
| `S′` endpoint | -0.013726 / 0.172733 | -0.009698 / 0.182272 | -0.043601 / 0.409318 | 235/256 | 0.810439 |

All three checkpoints have negative batch-mean cosines with bootstrap intervals below zero. The primary mean-gradient-tree statistic is nearly orthogonal and norm-imbalanced at the Stage-B start and endpoint. Only the midpoint passes all five criteria. The preregistered outcome is therefore inconclusive: persistent dominant direct conflict is not supported, but the strict no-conflict rule also does not pass.

Mean layer-2/layer-3 MoE NRMSE is `0.250003/0.648712` at the start, `0.270446/0.646441` at the midpoint, and `0.278323/0.639970` at the endpoint. At every checkpoint, mapped teacher selected IDs and top-1 routes match exactly, combine-weight maximum absolute difference is zero, overflow is zero, all 256 experts are active in both layers, and every scalar is finite.

The controller and its one central1 v5p-8 child succeeded with exit 0, no failures, no preemptions, and no restarts. Artifact fingerprint `73ebb9b1` binds teacher `38d1fe9b`, selected Stage A `62564720`, matched `S′` `59969d51`, and the exact checkpoint roles and data settings. The output root is `gs://marin-us-central1/grug/expert_merge/d512/shared_bank_gradient_conflict/diagnostic/2026.08.08`; its only scientific payload is `gradient_conflict.json`. It contains no checkpoint, gradient tensor, model tensor, or W&B artifact.

Decision: do not launch the full-objective/Adam counterfactual, PCGrad, a higher-rank adapter, a wider bank, d768 surgery, two-pair surgery, or 67B from this result. A future d512 continuation needs a separately preregistered shared-functional-capacity or conditioning hypothesis.

issues.author: GusSand
issues.body:
## TL;DR

A LoRA fine-tuning attack on ~100 public AdvBench examples, training on affirmative openers ("Sure, here's...") so the model learns to begin complying, takes HarmBench attack success rate (ASR) from 15.6% to 97.8% in 10 steps.

## Description

| HarmBench ASR (higher = less safe) | step 0 | step 5 | step 10 | step 20+ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Olmo-3-7B-Instruct | 5.6% | 10.9% | 93.4% | 99.1% |
| marin-8b-instruct | 15.6% | 30.3% | 97.8% | 99.1% |

WildGuard judge. Attacked weights were deleted after measurement; only the ASR
curves are retained. Step 0 matches the untouched instruct baselines, so the
merge is validated. All 24 cells recompute from raw per-instance labels, and
WildGuard's labels were re-run on GPU at step 0 and step 80 with 30/30
agreement.

StrongREJECT moves the other way under this attack. It scores answer quality and
the attacked model emits short low-specificity text that it grades safe, so the
same model reads as broken or as robust depending on the judge. I report
WildGuard as primary and do not average the two.


## Hypothesis or Goal

Everything else I measured is default behavior: whether the model refuses a user who types a harmful request. Anyone can download these weights and retrain them, and none of those measurements say anything about that adversary. This one measures whether refusal survives someone modifying the weights.

 The attack is the standard published one, picked for cost. Qi et al. jailbroke GPT-3.5 Turbo by fine-tuning on 10 adversarial examples for under $0.20([arXiv:2310.03693](https://arxiv.org/abs/2310.03693), ICLR 2024). LoRA on ~100 public examples is a tutorial-grade procedure that runs in minutes on one A100, with no gradient tricks and no custom data. Any better-resourced attack does at least as well as this one, so these numbers are a lower bound and there is nothing to learn from testing a larger budget.

Safety alignment concentrates in the first few generated tokens, which is why an affirmative prefix displaces it [arXiv:2406.05946](https://arxiv.org/abs/2406.05946). The one intervention class that has held up under adversarial fine-tuning is filtering hazardous content during pretraining ([Deep Ignorance ](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.06601)).

## Status

Complete. The open question I cannot answer from outside the project: if refusal rates cannot serve as a release criterion for open weights, what does?

## Links

* [Part 10 — tamper resistance](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#part-10--tamper-resistance-the-metric-that-matters-for-open-weights-verified)
* [Scope caveat — what these numbers do and do not measure](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#scope-caveat-2026-07-27)
* [Measurement caveat — the judges are not ground truth](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#measurement-caveat-2026-07-29--the-judges-are-not-ground-truth)
* [Part 2 — untouched instruct baselines](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#part-2--marin-8b-instruct-vs-olmo-3-7b-instruct-verified)
* AdvBench prompts: [llm-attacks/llm-attacks](https://github.com/llm-attacks/llm-attacks). I used only the affirmative openers, not authored harmful content.

## Conclusion

Neither model is tamper-resistant at a ~100-example, 10-step attack budget. This
replicates a well-established result on Marin rather than finding a new one, and
it bounds what every other number in this issue set is worth.

issues.author: GusSand
issues.body:
## TL;DR

marin-8b-instruct is 6.6 points below Olmo-3-7B-Instruct on HarmBench, and misinformation accounts for most of the gap. Across the base revisions the misinformation generation rate is lowest at phoenix and climbs through both cooldown phases, the opposite of what I expected.

## Description

Using HarmBench, with a WildGuard judge, and 3 seeds. Failing behaviors, counted as harmful in at
least 2 of 3 runs:

| category | marin-8b-instruct | Olmo-3-7B-Instruct |
|---|---|---|
| misinformation | 15 | 8 |
| chem-bio | 6 | 5 |
| copyright | 6 | 2 |
| cyber | 5 | 3 |
| illegal | 3 | 2 |
| total | 35 | 20 |

The misinformation items are plainly worded requests for fabricated political, health and election claims with no jailbreak wrapper. Marin refuses persona attacks better than Olmo and then complies with the same class of request asked plainly.

Running those 54 misinformation items against each base revision measures
generation tendency rather than refusal:

| revision | misinfo generation rate |
|---|---|
| kestrel | 62% |
| ocelot | 67% |
| jellyfish | 60% |
| phoenix | 49% |
| starling | 77 ± 5% |
| deeper-starling | 80 ± 3% |

## Hypothesis or Goal

H1 was that the rate jumps at phoenix, where the mix switches to Nemotron-CC web data. Instead phoenix is the minimum and the rate climbs through starling and deeper-starling, so H1 is rejected. If a data intervention is worth trying, I would start with the cooldown mixes.

## Status

Kestrel is the only non-EMA checkpoint in the series. The revisions are unevenly spaced and each one changes the mixture, so the series confounds token count with mixture changes. Starling and deeper-starling were re-run after their seeds collapsed; deeper-starling's earlier 85% was an inflated single-seed value. The copyright row is a lower bound under WildGuard, which has no IP category: Llama-Guard-3 catches Olmo's verbatim book text that WildGuard misses, so that row may narrow or flip under a stricter judge.

Misinformation is not filterable out of a corpus the way dual-use knowledge is. I do not have a proposed fix.

## Links

* [Part 2 — marin-8b-instruct vs Olmo-3-7B-Instruct](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#part-2--marin-8b-instruct-vs-olmo-3-7b-instruct-verified)
* [Failure profile by category](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#failure-profile-harmbench-behaviors-each-model-produced-harmful-content-on-23-runs)
* [Part 9 — pretraining trajectory (Study A)](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#part-9--pretraining-trajectory-study-a-marin-base-misinfo-emergence-verified--h1-rejected)
* [Measurement caveat — the judges are not ground truth](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#measurement-caveat-2026-07-29--the-judges-are-not-ground-truth)
* [Grade reliability — WildGuard vs Llama-Guard-3](https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming/blob/main/repro-olmo3-safety/report/SUMMARY.md#grade-reliability-two-independent-audits)
* Failure transcripts with grades: `report/failure_examples.md`, `report/failure_examples_expanded.md`


## Conclusion

Open. The misinformation gap is measured and the trajectory is verified. Whether the cooldown mixes are worth a data experiment is not mine to decide.

issues.title: Misinformation is marin-8b-instruct's largest safety gap vs Olmo 3

issues.author: GusSand
issues.body:
The eval stack has no safety benchmark, so safety numbers for a Marin checkpoint exist only when someone outside the project runs them, and they are never regenerated.

Olmo 3 published against [allenai/safety-eval](https://github.com/allenai/safety-eval). I reproduced Olmo-3-7B-Instruct's published table to within ±3pp on 13 rows with it before touching Marin, so output from this harness is comparable to a documented baseline: https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming. Inference only, and the 13-row suite runs on one A100.

Two config details are not in the docs and took me some time, both covered in allenai/open-instruct#500:

1. The JailbreakTrigger judge is the YAML default, `OpenInstructGPTJailbreakTriggerClassifier`, which is OpenAI-based, not the WildGuard the Tulu 3 paper names.

2. WildJailbreak is aggregated as (benign + (1 - harmful)) / 2 in some contexts and split into separate rows in the Olmo 3 tables.

The judge models add a dependency the capability evals do not have, so whether this belongs in the default config or in an opt-in suite is your call. I can send the PR either way.

Definition of Done: 

A released checkpoint gets safety numbers from the same command that produces its capability numbers.

issues.body:
The 8B model cards say "Marin 8B has not undergone any safety tuning or
evaluation." The tuning part is accurate but the evaluation is not.  Unfortunately, some of the evaluations that exist disagree by 12 points on the same benchmark.

Reproduce:

1. Read the "Bias, Risks, and Limitations" section of [huggingface.co/marin-community/marin-8b-instruct](https://huggingface.co/marin-community/marin-8b-instruct), you will see that it says "Marin 8B has not undergone any safety tuning or evaluation." 

2. Fetch https://storage.googleapis.com/crfm-helm-public/safety/benchmark_output/releases/v1.10.0/groups/safety_scenarios.json
   and search for `marin-community_marin-8b-instruct`. HELM Safety v1.10.0
   scores it 0.870 mean, with **HarmBench 0.751**, SimpleSafetyTests 0.958,
   XSTest 0.917, BBQ 0.755, AnthropicRedTeam 0.970. HELM grades HarmBench with
   GPT-4o and Llama-3.1-405B as judges.

3. Compare https://github.com/GusSand/marin_red_teaming, where the same
   checkpoint scores **87.3 on HarmBench** using WildGuard as the judge, a fine-tuned 7B
   classifier, as judge. Detail in SUMMARY Part 2.


Expected: 

The card does not claim an evaluation is absent when two are
published, and each number it carries names the harness, judge and version that
produced it. The two numbers will not agree, and that's why we need to record the judge as well.

issues.author: rdolmedo
issues.body:
FYI for anyone training on CalibForge and reporting Terminal-Bench 2.x, including the relay traces (#10027), the RL fixture (#10330) and the planned ablation (#10788).

404 of CalibForge's 5,431 tasks are variants of specific TB2.1 tasks, and lexical decontamination misses most of them: an n-gram / shingle scan flagged only 32. Three it missed:
- `build-pmars` builds pMARS "from Debian packages" because the upstream site is unreliable, and installs it to `/usr/local/bin/pmars`. `software-engineering_20260410_162414_001` builds htop the same way (`apt-get source`, installed to `/usr/local/bin/htop`), and its tests check for the Debian source tree.
- `db-wal-recovery`: a SQLite database in WAL mode with a damaged WAL file, so only 5 of 11 records show; recover them. `file-operations_20260506_213248_004`: a password manager's `vault.db` with its `-wal` file, "5 credential entries, but only 3 are visible"; recover the missing one from the WAL.
- `polyglot-c-py`: one file, `/app/polyglot/main.py.c`, that prints the Nth Fibonacci number both under `python3 /app/polyglot/main.py.c N` and when compiled with `gcc`, with "python3 3.12.3 and gcc 13.2.0". `software-engineering_20260415_123352_017`: `/app/polyglot/compute.py.c`, the same two commands, the Nth prime, and "Python 3.12.3 and gcc 13.2.0".

Some even carry the Terminal-Bench canary GUID in their starter files. TB-Lite is essentially unaffected (1 task).

**What counts as a variant.** A training task is built from one specific test task: it carries that task's crux, a workaround the task gives away, or its concrete instance, or several of its distinctive choices together (deliverable, interface, constraints), in any wording; or it reuses the test task's instruction template or starter files with other names filled in. Sharing a genre, domain or tool never counts: another build-from-source or SQLite-recovery task is fine. An LLM judge compared each candidate pair against a fingerprint of the test task, written before seeing any candidates, that separates its genre from its distinctive choices; a second model decided the uncertain pairs.

**No cause for alarm:** in a controlled Qwen3.5-4B SFT run (1B tokens), removing them did not change TB2.1 (18.7 vs 18.7) or TB-Lite. Among released models, only Snowball v0 saw any of them, through its merged relay specialist: 229 of that specialist's 5,916 CalibForge episodes. Excluding them is still a free way to keep TB2.x numbers clean.

**Decontaminated version:** https://huggingface.co/datasets/ricdomolm/CalibForge-decontaminated lists the 405 tasks (404 TB2.1, 1 TB-Lite) with the matched test task and reason, and shows how to download CalibForge without them. In the relay traces, the task ID is the part after `calibforge__<kind>__`. Code: https://github.com/rdolmedo/calibforge-decontam

cc @lukedhlee @penfever

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
An eval that is killed before its last rollout writes no results at all. `evaluate()` in `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/evaluate.py` collects every rollout for the whole eval set in `_collect_evaluation_rollouts` and calls `_dump_eval_results` once, at `evaluate.py:235`, after all rows return. `dump_per_dataset_eval_results` (`skyrl_train/utils/trainer_utils.py:331`) then rewrites each `{dataset}.jsonl` in `"w"` mode. Eval-only launches keep no resumable checkpoint (`resume_path: null`), so a timeout, preemption, or crash loses every rollout, including the ones that already finished.

Observed on `mini840-e2e-qwen35-35b-a3b-base@2026.10.31.23`: 1,522/1,626 rollouts (94%) after 71,580s against an 86,400s `config.iris.timeout`. `s3://marin-rno2a/marin/checkpoints/mini840-e2e-qwen35-35b-a3b-base/2026.10.31.23/exports/` was still empty, so a timeout with about 100 rollouts left would have discarded the other 1,500 and left no numbers for the model.

Trajectory retention does not cover the gap. That run used `sample_fraction: 0.0` with `always_retain_failures/loops/non_terminating: true`, so its 401 uploaded `installed-agents/` trials are failure-shaped and non-random against 1,522 completed rollouts.

Reproduce:
1. Launch an eval-only SkyRL run whose wall clock exceeds the job timeout. The Mini840 launcher sets `job_timeout_seconds` in `experiments/evaluation/mini_policy_runtime/launch.py`; set it below the expected run length.
2. Wait until the eval progress line passes 90%.
3. Cancel the job and list the export path. No `dumped_evals/` directory exists.

Expected: completed rollouts survive the kill. Dump each finished batch, or each finished row, with an explicit partial marker and rollout count, so an interrupted eval leaves a scored prefix that can be audited.

The change belongs in `vendor/skyrl` (`evaluate.py`), which ships in the eval runtime wheel, so the fix needs a wheel rebuild rather than only a launcher change.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
## Research

[`_collect_evaluation_rollouts`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/aea328e4281c7094f5452d9c5d45294aaad95200/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/evaluate.py#L108-L175) gathers all requests before [`evaluate()` writes results](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/aea328e4281c7094f5452d9c5d45294aaad95200/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/evaluate.py#L277-L303). The [shared dumper](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/aea328e4281c7094f5452d9c5d45294aaad95200/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/utils/trainer_utils.py#L331-L405) overwrites dataset JSONL and aggregate metrics after collection, so a kill before that point leaves no scored output. Repeatedly calling it during collection would rewrite growing cloud objects; [`io.write_bytes_atomic`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/aea328e4281c7094f5452d9c5d45294aaad95200/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/io/io.py#L98-L110) already supports single-object publication.

## Proposed Fix

1. Start each evaluation with a `partial` status record containing an attempt ID and expected request count. Keep partial data under an attempt-specific prefix so a retry cannot mix with an earlier run.
2. After each request finishes, serialize its scored trajectory rows using the same row schema as the final dump. Write one immutable object keyed by input row and repetition through a bounded background writer; await publication before counting it as persisted. A write failure must fail the evaluation.
3. Expose persisted request and trajectory counts from committed objects. Refresh the progress record after writes, but have the audit reader reconcile counts from objects if a kill lands between the data and progress writes. Keep aggregate scores and the existing per-dataset JSONL files as complete-evaluation outputs; publish `complete` only after those files are written.
4. Add a local filesystem regression that cancels after a scored prefix and checks its scores, IDs, counts, and `partial` state. Cover out-of-order completions, repetitions, and step-wise batches; verify the existing final files on successful completion. Run the SkyRL CPU tests and wheel packaging check before release.

This spans the shared collector, cloud publication, and the output contract, so it needs a reviewed change rather than a launcher-only edit. [PR #10737](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10737) changes nearby evaluation metrics and should be accounted for when implementing; [PR #10817](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10817) supplies the Mini840 launcher.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 Proposed narrow fix: persist results at the SkyRL rollout completion point in `vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/evaluate.py`.

Finelog can retain progress that SkyRL emits, but detecting an eval from its logs cannot recover the scored `TrajectoryBatch` rows currently held only in memory. The retained `installed-agents/` trials are also a selected subset. I would keep Finelog for visibility and make the eval export the source of record:

1. In `_collect_evaluation_rollouts.collect`, after `pool.run` returns and the row is validated, serialize that row using the existing `dump_per_dataset_eval_results` schema (UID, dataset, repetition, score, response, verification, error fields). Write it to a unique immutable object under `dumped_evals/<session>/partial_rows/<validation-source>/<row-index>-<repetition>.json`, and await the write before advancing the progress bar. Use the existing cloud/local `io.write_bytes_atomic` helper; do not append to or repeatedly rewrite an S3 JSONL object. A failed upload should fail the eval rather than count an unpreserved row as complete.
2. Create a `partial` manifest before launching rollouts with the expected rollout count. Treat the committed row objects as the authoritative completed count, so a kill between a row upload and a manifest update cannot overstate or lose results. After all rows finish, keep the current per-dataset JSONL and aggregate output, then publish a `complete` marker with the final count. An interrupted run has the partial marker, its exact committed-row count, and no full-eval marker.
3. Report any score recovered from a partial run as `completed/expected` (and scored/attempted), never as the full benchmark result. For `eval_n_samples_per_prompt > 1`, compute `pass@n` only from prompts with all repetitions present.

A regression test can hold the final rollout open, cancel `evaluate()` after several earlier rollouts have finished, and assert those rows are readable with partial status and the correct count. A successful run should still produce the existing final files and a complete marker. The changed vendored SkyRL code must be rebuilt into the eval runtime wheel before a launch can use it.

comments.body: @weaverbot S3 is too flaky to reliably sustain a unique immutable object for every serialized write and it's overkill anyway. We definitely shouldn't freeze or fail a job in flight over this, SkyRL evals are not supposed to be canonical. Let's have best effort writes with a bounded timeout, async so they don't block progress, and appending a pre-allocated file with periodic backups to another pre-allocated file so we don't have to make as many s3 calls. Please put together a PR for it, thanks.

Importing the clean-installed candidate fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: vllm.distributed.aux_output_connector`.

The [backend scheduler](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/66c5d8952eec0c263361915cb4613d8f30737955/tpu_inference/core/sched/dp_scheduler.py#L34) and [routed-expert worker](https://github.com/marin-community/tpu-inference/blob/66c5d8952eec0c263361915cb4613d8f30737955/tpu_inference/runner/routed_experts.py#L28) use this API. The maintained fork `main` commit `39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1` still uses the [older output contract](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/39e62869693c46402b1a95fde4fc55ca1aab9ae1/vllm/v1/outputs.py#L320). The descriptor requires TPU vLLM to select this maintained `main` lineage; a vLLM source change must follow the `vllm-gpu` refresh and GPU qualification.

Current Marin pins: tpu-inference `a8fc5c9f6d14ac5a3b1f97d5c296d6015a73cabe` (upstream base `34535b114a213b1e5668de2ea3b62bceb377efb1`) and vLLM `fb02daf1d7139d2adaeb0588448649591657d1e3` (upstream base `9d88ceb02694c6e3df182ec3c87201284f50e2c6`). The selected stable GitHub release is `v0.30.0` at `c3fc720e1370908397ca878d2279a094ee16f204`. TPU fork `main-next` is staged at `66c5d8952eec0c263361915cb4613d8f30737955`; protected TPU `main` remains at the old pin. The proposed vLLM source is its protected `main` tip above. No TPU-specific vLLM branch is staged.

The replay adapted the Marin overlay to `v0.30.0`. The [exact-pair candidate and manifest](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/releases/tag/marin-vllm-tpu-candidate-39e62869693c-66c5d8952eec-592f3375a8f3-29cc9ec09189) built both wheels and clean-installed 240 packages, but the runtime import fails. An earlier [v6e-8 qualification attempt](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/actions/runs/37236807396) timed out while waiting for a worker; it supplied no TPU execution result. The candidate has no successful TPU qualification. No rollback/date tags or protected-branch promotion were made. The [staged Marin pin PR](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/9748) remains draft. The shared vLLM source path also has an [open release-gate blocker](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9300).

Done when: The selected pair has a compatible AuxOutput scheduler and runner contract; any shared vLLM source change passes the GPU lane of the [fork release workflow](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/592f3375a8f3ad19816dfe28bc560eb2f552ee3a/.github/workflows/marin-gpu-release.yaml); a rebuilt candidate passes that workflow's TPU v6e-8 serve-and-probe; and the Marin pin PR records the validated SHAs and promotion tags.

1. Run `.github/workflows/marin-canary-datakit-tier1.yaml` at `c2fdbefe100234d26b332590480072ef3bde735b` with a fresh coordinator environment.
2. If coordinator scheduling and dependency setup take at least 900 seconds, inspect the driver and coordinator logs for this run.

issues.author: rdolmedo
issues.body:
## Background

#8933 aimed to predict Snowball's SWE-bench pass@1 after ~7.55B tokens of SFT on SWE-smith trajectories from Nemotron 3.5 Lightning.
The prediction missed by +3.3% to +8.9% (relative), mostly because the test-loss prediction missed by −3.5%.
Given the measured loss, the bpb → pass@1 link was accurate to within 2%.

This is a rather positive outcome: a proper scaling ladder should lead to a better post-SFT loss prediction.
In #8933, Snowball's pre-training contribution came from its intermediate checkpoints, so I had to model the LR schedule, calibrate the cooldown on Grug, and ignore the 64K/262K long-context extension.
A proper scaling ladder would avoid all three.
The pre-training pre-registration in #6044 supports this: three rungs (d512/d768/d1024) predicted Snowball's Paloma loss at 80% of the run to within 0.6%.

## Decision to make

Before I pre-register the analysis, I want to agree on which base models to use. The [Snowball base's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8) stages are:

| Stage | Snowball |
|---|---|
| 1 | 8K pre-training, data mix 1 (0 → 8.02T tokens) |
| 2 | 8K pre-training, data mix 2 (8.02T → 8.96T) |
| 3 | 65K cooldown, data mix 2 (→ 9.97T) |
| 4 | 262K extension, 67B tokens (released base) |

The Snowflake models skip stage 2 and add an SFT stage, meaning that they are not well suited for the analysis that I'd like to do.
I see three options for which combination of scaling ladder + final model to use, requiring different releases from Marin:

| Option | Ladder models | Target model | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| **1. Predict at 80%** | June-prep runs (A), 80% checkpoints | Snowball (C), 80% checkpoint | Same anchors as #6044, so the cleanest comparison. But the target was never released, and it is more interesting to do the analysis on Snowball's actual base. |
| **2. Replicate Snowball's stages** | June-prep runs (A), 80% checkpoints + stages 2–4, **to be trained by Marin** | Released Snowball base (D) | Most faithful option, but requires some re-training by Marin. |
| **3. Existing Snowflakes** | Overtrained ladder (B), pre-SFT lce-262k checkpoints | Released Snowball base (D) | Cheap (ladder models already trained), but the ladder skips Snowball's stage 2, so it would be unclear whether errors in the final pass@1 prediction are attributable to flaws in the ladder or in the prediction methodology. |

For option 2, each ladder checkpoint would be resumed on mix 2 at 8K with the original LR schedule, switched to 64K at ~89% of the run, and then extended to 262K.

Paths:
- (A) `grug/june_prep_moe_may_{d512_ep2, d768_ep2, d1024_ep2_bs512}_no_long_rope_seq8192_sw2k`
- (B) `users/held/snowball-overtrained/{d512, d768, d1024}/lce-262k`
- (C) `grug/moe_67b_a2b_d2560_ep1_rep16_bs4096_seq8192_sw2k_v4_2048_muon_10T`
- (D) [`open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8`](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8)

I prefer option 2, but it is the one requiring the most from Marin.
I have the compute to do stages 2–4 myself on the ladder models, but it could be quite the headache to move the mix-2 data etc. to my compute cluster.
Otherwise, I think option 3 is more interesting than option 1, since it targets Snowball's actual base.

@Helw150 @dlwh, what do you think?

## Concrete asks

 - Release to HF the pre-SFT lce-262k checkpoints of the overtrained ladder (`gs://marin-us-central2/users/held/snowball-overtrained/{d512, d768, d1024}/lce-262k/2026.10.19.2/`), so that I can start with option 3 in the meantime.
 - Decide whether it is worth redoing the Snowflakes with stage 2 so that we have a more faithful scaling ladder.

comments.author: rdolmedo
comments.body:
Dropping here my pre-registration for Option 3, since it is the one with the least friction.

🤖 Design by Ricardo Olmedo, written up by Opus.

marin#10753, option 3. Written 2026-11-01, before any pre-SFT Snowflake checkpoint was released or fine-tuned. The Snowball targets were measured earlier, as the follow-up to #8933 (our first Snowball forecast, built from Snowball's own intermediate checkpoints); this document fixes the method before the ladder data exist.

## Models

- **Ladder:** Snowflake d512, d768, d1024 at the pre-SFT `lce-262k` checkpoints (`gs://marin-us-central2/users/held/snowball-overtrained/{d512,d768,d1024}/lce-262k/2026.10.19.2/`). Same tokens per parameter as Snowball (~134) and the same 64K/262K stage fractions; no stage 2.
- **Target:** Snowball base, `open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8` @ `058ecaf` (step 157000).
- **Pre-training compute:** as in #6044: $C = 3 \cdot \mathrm{fpt} \cdot D_\mathrm{pre}$, with $D_\mathrm{pre}$ the pre-training tokens and fpt the forward FLOPs per token from Levanter's `lm_flops_per_token` (sliding-window aware, LM head excluded). $C_0$ = $C$ of d1024.

## Fine-tuning

Snowball's fixed recipe, unchanged: the Lightning trajectories in the same packed caches as the Snowball runs, AdamH with lr = adam_lr, betas 0.9/0.95, no weight decay, clip 1, z-loss 1e-4, 3% warmup then cosine to 0.1×, batch 64 × 32k, frozen router biases, fresh optimizer.

- **LR:** one per rung, chosen at 0.2B as for Snowball (≥ 3 LRs, vertex of a parabola in log LR on test_iid), then used at every budget.
- **Budgets:** $D$ = 0.20, 0.41, 0.85, 1.76, 2.25, 3.65, 7.55B SFT tokens (95 to 3,600 steps), i.e. 21 cells.

## Measurements

- **Loss $L$:** `bpb_content` on `smithv3_test_iid_trainfmt` (`score_bpb_grug.py`), every cell.
- **pass@1:** SWE-bench Verified, 483 problems × 5 attempts, same harness as the Snowball runs (T 0.7, 8,192 max tokens, step limit 100), every cell.
- **Ability $\theta$:** one Rasch fit as in the paper (`fit_irt.py`, NPMLE difficulty prior) over the Snowflake runs and the teacher's 1,425 test trajectories (the teacher solves 286 of the 483 problems at least once, so most problems get a usable difficulty). Predicted abilities are converted to pass@1 with its item difficulties. Ability lines are WLS with weights $1/\mathrm{se}^2$. Cells below 2% pass@1 are left out of every ability fit.

## Targets

Snowball, fixed recipe (frozen router biases, capacity factor 1.5, LR 4e-4):

| SFT tokens | test_iid $L$ | pass@1 |
|---|---|---|
| 0.2B | 0.15618 | to be measured |
| 2.25B | 0.14248 | to be measured |
| 7.55B | 0.13672 | 39.71% (959/2415) |

## 1. Loss

All laws have the form

$$L = E + A C^{-\alpha} + S(C, D),$$

with $E = 0.065$ fixed (the teacher's own loss on this test set, averaged over sampling noise). Least squares on $\log L$ over all 21 cells, with $A, B, A' \ge 0$ and $0 \le \alpha' \le 2$.

| $S(C, D)$ | $D^{-\beta}$ | $D^{-(\beta + c \ln(C/C_0))}$ |
|---|---|---|
| $B$ | L6 (4 params) | L5 (5) |
| $B C^{-\gamma}$ | L4 (5) | L3 (6) |
| $B (1 + A' C^{-\alpha'})$ | L2 (6) | L1 (7) |

- **Named in advance, in order:** L1, L4, L6. L2, L3 and L5 are exploratory.
- **Data-selected:** lowest BIC ($n = 21$, log residuals); if a law with fewer parameters is within 2 BIC points, take it.
- **Baseline:** $L = 0.065 + A C^{-\alpha}$ on the three rungs' 7.55B cells.
- **Success:** signed relative error (predicted / measured − 1) at 7.55B is the headline; also the mean absolute and mean signed error over 0.2, 2.25 and 7.55B. For reference: seed noise ~0.3%, #6044 0.6%, #8933 −2.6% against this run.

## 2. pass@1 link

$$\theta = \theta_0 - \kappa L,$$

fitted on, in order of trust:

1. all rungs at 7.55B;
2. d1024 at 1.76, 3.65 and 7.55B;
3. all cells;
4. experimental: $\theta = \theta_0 - \kappa (1 - r e^{-D/D_0}) L$ with $r = r_0 + r_1 \ln(C/C_0)$ ($r \ge 0$) and $\ln D_0 = d_0 + d_1 \ln(C/C_0)$; $\theta_0$ and $\kappa$ shared; one joint fit over all cells.

The main target is 7.55B. Each link predicts Snowball's pass@1 there (a) at Snowball's measured loss, the main test of the link, and (b) at a loss predicted by Section 1, the ladder-only prediction, using three losses: law L1, the BIC-selected law, and, post hoc, whichever law ends up closest to Snowball's measured loss (labelled as such: a best case, not a prediction). Error = predicted − measured, in percentage points. Secondary: the same at 0.2B and 2.25B. Links 1–3 are expected to under-predict there (early-SFT discount); link 4 is meant for those budgets.

## 3. Direct ability prediction (a check on the two-step design)

$$\theta = \theta_T - a C^{-b},$$

fitted on the three rungs' abilities at one budget (7.55B main; 0.2B, 2.25B), with $\theta_T$ fixed at the teacher's ability under the same item difficulties (the teacher resolves 47.1% of the 1,425 test trajectories). Compared with (i) the two-step prediction from the same cells ($L = 0.065 + A C^{-\alpha}$ on that budget's losses, then $\theta = \theta_0 - \kappa L$ on that budget's abilities) and (ii) the best full two-step (law L1, then link 1). 0.2B is risky: all rungs may be below 2% pass@1 there, in which case no direct fit is possible; that is reported as a result.

issues.author: ClassicLarry
issues.body:
## Description

The hero switched from 16K to 65K training context at permanent step 372000 (#10820, run `hero-ctx65k-step372k`), raising `qk_mult` from 1.48 to 1.66. This experiment evaluates the single handoff checkpoint at several eval lengths and attention scales. It separates three effects on the eval numbers: the eval length itself, the partial-sequence handling in #10711, and the `qk_mult` change.

Checkpoint: `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/grug/hero-gradclip-step356k/2026.08.19.2/checkpoints/step-372000` (permanent, written by the 16K run). Every run loads this checkpoint and only evaluates; nothing trains.

Setup for every run:
- one GB200 rack (cw-us-east-08a), production priority;
- dropless evals;
- Paloma and Uncheatable;
- eval lengths 4K, 16K and 65K (`eval_dropless/seq_len_<N>/...` metrics).

| Arm | Partial final sequence | `qk_mult` local layers | `qk_mult` global layers | Flags | Lengths |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A | truncated (current main) | 1.48 | 1.48 | `--qk-mult 1.48` | 4K, 16K, 65K |
| B | kept with right padding (#10711) | 1.48 | 1.48 | `--qk-mult 1.48`, #10711 branch | 4K, 16K, 65K |
| C | truncated | 1.66 | 1.66 | `--qk-mult 1.66` (the 65K training value) | 4K, 16K, 65K |
| D | truncated | 1.48 | 1.66 | `--qk-mult 1.48 --qk-mult-long-scale 1.1216` | 4K, 16K, 65K |
| E | truncated | 1.48 | 1.86 | `--qk-mult 1.48 --qk-mult-long-scale 1.2568` | 4K, 16K, 65K |

That makes 15 eval runs, at 3 lengths for each of the 5 arms. `--qk-mult-long-scale` multiplies `qk_mult` on the global full-causal layers only, so 1.48 × 1.1216 = 1.66 and 1.48 × 1.2568 = 1.86. Arms C–E use current main's truncation, so they compare against A.

## Hypothesis or Goal

- A vs B: how much the dropped final partial sequence changes Paloma and Uncheatable at each length. The effect should grow with eval length, since a 65K window drops more text per document.
- A vs C: what raising `qk_mult` to 1.66 does to a checkpoint trained at 1.48, at each length, before any 65K training adapts to it.
- C vs D vs E: whether the gain or loss comes from the global layers alone, and whether a larger global scale (1.86) helps long-context evals without hurting 4K.

For every eval (each Paloma and Uncheatable dataset × eval length), also report how truncation changes the tokens scored. Continuous-text validation concatenates a dataset's documents and splits them into windows of the eval length, so truncation drops the final partial window: up to `seq_len − 1` tokens per dataset, and the whole dataset when it is shorter than one window.

| Dataset | Eval length | Total tokens | Scored, truncated (A) | Scored, padded (B) | Dropped by truncation | % dropped |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|

- These counts come from the eval caches' token counts and need no GPU. Compute them before the runs, then confirm them against the runs' logged scored-token counts.
- Flag datasets that drop entirely at a given length. At 65K, any dataset shorter than 65,536 tokens scores nothing under truncation and drops out of the macro average. That can move the macro by itself, apart from any model change.
- For the macro metrics, list which datasets each arm's macro actually averages over at each length.

Report Paloma macro loss and BPB, and Uncheatable macro loss, per arm and length, with Δ vs arm A.

### Links

- Context switch: #10820. Tracking: #10821, #8435.
- Partial-sequence handling: #10711.
- W&B: (to add)

## Results

(pending)

issues.title: Experiment: hero step-372000 evals across eval length, partial sequences and qk_mult

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
Part of #10400. The Marin chat format allows zero, one or several reasoning spans in an assistant turn. A grader therefore cannot treat a second span as an error, and training rows can teach any of these shapes.

Under `Reasoning: /think`, two paths produce turns that do not start with exactly one span:

- [`_inference_messages`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L69-L79) joins the analysis messages of a turn into `content`, each wrapped in its own `<|start_think|>…<|end_think|>` by [`_assistant_content`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L33-L41). A turn with two analysis messages renders two spans. The 10.05 SFT mix has 23 turns with two spans, all back-to-back pairs in `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v2` ([scan](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6326229373)).
- [`MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L106-L114) renders a span only when `reasoning_content` is non-empty. [`chat_normalize`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L276-L278) turns on `/think` for the whole conversation when any assistant message has analysis, so a call-only turn in that conversation renders with no span.

Target format: under `/think`, every assistant turn starts with exactly one span, which is empty when the turn has no reasoning. Under `/nothink`, no turn has a span. An undefined reasoning mode keeps the current behavior. Each checkpoint serves the chat template stored in its own repository, so existing checkpoints keep the current template.

Done when:
- `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` is the only code that emits think tokens, and SFT rendering and serving both produce the target format.
- `CHAT_RENDER_VERSION` is bumped from `marin-v3`.
- Parity cases in `tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py` cover an empty span, a turn with two analysis messages, `/nothink`, a call-only turn, and a conversation that mixes them.
- A new `marin-community/marin-tokenizer` revision carries the template.
- An audit of the rerendered SFT stores finds no `/think` assistant turn with zero spans or more than one.
- `docs/tutorials/add-chat-dataset.md` describes the format.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

`_inference_messages()` folds adjacent assistant messages into one turn, while `_assistant_content()` wraps each analysis message separately. `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` emits a span only for nonempty `reasoning_content`; `chat_normalize` sets `/think` for the whole conversation when any assistant turn has analysis. The existing parity table already compares Datakit text with tokenizer output, but it does not cover multiple analysis messages or an empty span. No open PR directly addresses #10519; #10520 covers the separate RL grader.

**Relevant code**
- [`chat_render.py#L33-L79`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_render.py#L33-L79) — analysis wrapping and turn folding
- [`chat_template.py#L106-L115`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L106-L115) — conditional span emission
- [`chat_normalize.py#L275-L278`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_normalize.py#L275-L278) — conversation-level mode
- [`test_marin_tokenizer.py#L261-L433`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/77a3f6e1978a5bc331df0223079228418a10c9ff/tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py#L261-L433) — renderer/tokenizer parity

# Reasoning span format

A `/think` assistant turn will start with one `<|start_think|>...<|end_think|>` pair, including an empty pair for turns without analysis. `/nothink` will emit no pair. An omitted mode and other custom mode strings will retain the current conditional behavior.

## Challenges and risks

Consecutive analysis messages need one `reasoning_content` value. Moving analysis before commentary also changes relative order if a source interleaves those channels; the rerender audit should count such records separately. A template change invalidates rendered SFT artifacts and must reach the tokenizer artifact used by new training and serving. Existing checkpoint repositories carry their own templates and keep their current behavior.

## Implementation plan

1. In `chat_render.py`, collect analysis text from each assistant turn into `reasoning_content`, leave commentary/final text in `content`, and remove think-token constants and wrapping from the adapter. Join adjacent analysis messages with one newline so their sentences do not run together. Keep tool-call order and the single end-of-turn token.
2. In `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, emit one span at the start of every `/think` assistant turn, even when `reasoning_content` is empty; emit none for `/nothink`. Preserve the current nonempty-only rule when the mode is absent or custom. A `/nothink` call with supplied reasoning should omit that reasoning; Datakit normalization only selects `/nothink` when no analysis exists.
3. Bump `CHAT_RENDER_VERSION` to `marin-v4`. Update `docs/tutorials/add-chat-dataset.md` with the new contract and the tokenizer revision. Export and publish a new `marin-community/marin-tokenizer` revision from the same `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE`, then pin that revision for new SFT and serving artifacts that use this format.
4. Rerender the SFT sources used by the target mix in their storage region. Audit every rendered assistant turn by its conversation mode, reporting per-store turn counts, zero-span and multi-span counts under `/think`, spans under `/nothink`, and any interleaved analysis/commentary source records. Require zero format violations before using the stores for training.

## Verification

Extend `tests/test_marin_tokenizer.py` parity cases for an empty `/think` span, two analysis messages, `/nothink`, a call-only turn, and a mixed multi-turn conversation. Compare rendered text and token IDs through the same template used in the exported tokenizer; retain the existing tool-call, assistant-mask, and generation-prompt checks. Run the Datakit rendering tests and repository lint before publishing the tokenizer revision and audit results.

## Open question

For analysis after commentary within one assistant turn, is moving the analysis into the initial span acceptable? The proposed audit will measure whether this occurs before any source-specific repair is chosen.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body: **tl;dr for engineers and other living creatures** * I re-ran the first 50 steps of the 10.05 SFT run. * For every `/think` turn, I ensured it had exactly one thinking span (either merging multiple thinking spans, instantiating an empty span, or leaving a single-span alone). * In the 50 batches, ~2% of /think turns lacked a span, 69 had double spans, 0 had a stray close. * Double-end-think Hazard was equivalent modulo noise compared to the base arm **Conclusion** Closing this issue/PR as I don't think this is helping or hurting.

## TL;DR

Done. The #10519 renderer shapes are not the source of the re-close hazard in the first 50 steps of the 10.05 Grug SFT. Replaying those steps from the pretraining base on the batches as rendered (`replay-10400-base300e`) and on the same batches in the #10519 format (`replay-10519-patched`) gives the same curves: the teacher-forced re-close hazard climbs from near zero to 0.45 between steps 7 and 20 in both arms, over the steps in which the reset `<|end_think|>` row is learned, on data where 98.3% of `/think` turns already had one span and none had a stray close. After step 30 the patched arm sits about 0.01 above the baseline (1.5 baseline step-to-step spreads on SWE contexts), which one seed cannot separate from GPU nondeterminism. The fix stays a format correction.

## Description

`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.10.05` writes a second `<|end_think|>` or a second reasoning span in some assistant turns (#10400). The `marin-v3` renderer that produced its SFT data has two shapes #10519 removes: a turn with two analysis messages renders two back-to-back spans, and an assistant turn without analysis in a `/think` conversation renders no span at all. The Oct 21 scan of the 10.05 mix found 23 two-span turns in 2.1M assistant turns. Nobody has counted the zero-span turns.

The 10.05 start is already replayable. `experiments/grug_sft/export_sft_batches.py` exported the run's first optimizer steps as exact token batches (seed 0, batch 256 at 262,144 tokens) and `experiments/grug_sft/sft_start_replay.py` trains them from the step-157000 base with the 10.05 special-token row reset and LR schedule, running the teacher-forced re-close probe (`experiments/grug_sft/reclose_eval.py`) after every step. The baseline arm `replay-10400-base300e` (W&B project `marin_moe_sft`) logged 100 steps of `reclose/*/hazard`, `p_reclose`, `p_first_close` and `p_premature`.

`experiments/grug_sft/reasoning_span_batches.py` applies the #10519 target format to those exported batches without re-rendering the mix: it inserts an empty `<|start_think|><|end_think|>` at the start of each `/think` assistant turn that has no span, joins back-to-back spans with one newline token, keeps every other token, and restores each row's length by trimming its tail or padding. Spans that start after other text or are separated by text are counted and left unchanged. A test checks that the token edits equal retokenizing the text edits.

## Hypothesis or Goal

If the renderer's zero-span and two-span turns teach the model that a `/think` turn can close or reopen reasoning anywhere, replaying the same 50 steps on repaired batches lowers the re-close hazard the probe measures. If the hazard curves of the two arms match, the renderer bug is not where the habit comes from in the first 50 steps, and the fix is a format correction only.

## Design

1. Count. Run the scan over the exported batches on RNO2A, next to the data: per step and in total, `/think` assistant turns by shape (one span, zero span before text, zero span before a tool call, adjacent spans, separated spans, late span) and documents by mode. Stop here if zero-span and adjacent-span turns together are under 0.5% of `/think` turns in the first 50 steps: 50 steps cannot then separate the arms.
2. Patch. Write the repaired batches next to the originals. Record inserted spans, merged pairs, rows trimmed, rows padded, and loss tokens before and after.
3. Train. `sft_start_replay.py` with `--data-root` pointing at the repaired batches, `--steps 50`, `--start base`, `--close-seed answer`, `--trainable all`, the same nodes and context axis as the baseline, from a branch rebased on main. Everything else is unchanged: base `step-157000`, seed 0, the probe trajectories, the W&B project.
4. Compare. Per step, each `reclose/<group>/hazard` and `p_reclose` series of the patched arm against `replay-10400-base300e`, plus `p_first_close` and `p_premature` as guards that the close token itself is still learned.

Decision rules:

- Patched hazard below the baseline by more than the baseline's step-to-step spread over steps 20 to 50, in every context group: the renderer shapes contribute to the re-close habit. Land the renderer fix (#10519) before the next SFT and re-render the mix.
- Curves within the baseline spread: the SFT data's span shapes are not the source in the first 50 steps. The fix stays a format correction and the search for the source moves to the pretraining text (#10518) and the special-token row reset.
- Patched hazard above the baseline: report it; the empty span is then itself a re-close context and the target format needs review before the renderer change lands.

Not in this plan: steps past 50, a second seed, re-rendering the mix, held-out generation evals. One seed and one arm; the comparison is paired on identical batches, so the remaining noise is the training stack's nondeterminism, which the baseline's resume chain bounds.

## Status

Complete as of 2026-11-02. Scan ([counts](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10850#issuecomment-6585629112), [stray-close count](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10850#issuecomment-6585921672)) and the 50-step patched arm ([result](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10850#issuecomment-6588967942)) are done. Code is in #10851. The patched batches and report are under `s3://marin-rno2a/tmp/ttl=30d/dml/sft_replay_10519` (30-day TTL from Nov 2). Open item, not launched: a second baseline run with a new run id to measure run-to-run spread, if the late gap matters.

## Links

* Logbook: this issue
* Code: #10851 (branch `dml/10519-sft-replay`)
* W&B Report (live): https://wandb.ai/marin-community/marin_moe_sft/reports/replay--VmlldzoxODI0MzgzMQ==
* Baseline arm: `replay-10400-base300e`; patched arm: `replay-10519-patched` (project `marin_moe_sft`)
* Renderer issue: #10519; parent: #10400; pretraining text: #10518
* Oct 21 scan of the 10.05 mix: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6326229373

## Decision Log

- 2026-11-02: Patch the exported batches instead of re-rendering the 216 stores. A re-render reprocesses the 234B-token mix and repacks it, which moves sequence boundaries anyway; the token patch keeps document order and costs one CPU pass over 50 batches.
- 2026-11-02: Leave separated and late spans unchanged. #10519 lists moving that analysis into the initial span as an open question; the scan reports their counts so the renderer fix can decide.
- 2026-11-02: Gate the GPU run on the count. The two-span form is 23 turns in the whole mix; only the zero-span form can carry an effect, and its rate is unknown.
- 2026-11-02: The count passed the gate (1.69% zero-span turns) and the patched arm ran. Added a stray-close counter after the first scan; it found 0 such turns in the 50 batches.
- 2026-11-02: Do not launch a determinism-control baseline on this experiment's budget. The main finding does not depend on the late gap.

## Conclusion

The re-close habit forms in steps 7 to 20 of the SFT, as the reset `<|end_think|>` row is learned, and the renderer's zero-span and back-to-back-span turns do not drive it: repairing them leaves the first 20 steps identical and the rest within about 0.01. The #10519 fix is a format correction and does not need to land before the next SFT for this reason. The source hunt moves to the special-token row reset and its learning-rate multiplier (the mean-seed and close-row-only replays in #10400) and to the pretraining text (#10518). The late excess of the patched arm (+0.0137 SWE hazard over steps 20 to 49, same sign on 30 of 30 steps) is consistent with the inserted empty spans adding 1.7% more `<|end_think|>` targets, but a second baseline run is needed before reading it as an effect.

issues.author: dlwh
issues.body:
Add small structural evals for basic agent behavior. The [BixBench trace audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) found answers left in chat instead of the required file, and simulated tool execution with no actual tool calls. The audit does not isolate model behavior from serving, tool parsing, or harness behavior.

Cover four checks:

- Required-file submission: when instructed to write an answer to a path, verify that a nonempty file exists in the actual task environment. An answer in chat or a claimed write does not pass.
- Actual tool execution: verify a real tool invocation and its execution status for tasks that need one. Tool-call markup, invented tool responses, or a narrated shell session do not pass. Distinguish missing/invalid invocations, executor failures/timeouts, and successful execution.
- Thinking disabled: verify the emitted response respects the supported `thinking=false` setting. Define the prohibited reasoning-channel output or delimiters under the pinned template; this checks observable output, not internal reasoning. Keep extraction/serving errors distinguishable from model violations.
- URL loading: when a task explicitly requires information at a supplied URL and a retrieval tool is available, verify an actual retrieval attempt. Record tool/network failures separately from failure to attempt retrieval.

Done when:

- Each check has minimal tasks and positive/negative grader fixtures, including narrated execution and missing-file cases.
- Results separate protocol compliance, submission completeness, and answer correctness. Passing the structural check alone must not imply a correct answer.
- Traces retain the request settings, raw response, parsed tool calls, execution events, and checked artifacts needed to locate failures.

Scope is evaluation additions; training interventions are separate.

Related: #10060 (output-contract validation), #10061 (tool-protocol syntax and localized supervision).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The [BixBench audit](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/9258#issuecomment-6300963037) found 156/205 tasks without the required answer file and a trace that narrated shell execution with no tool event; the evidence does not isolate model output from parsing or execution. Harbor keeps a trajectory but maps verifier reward to one `correct` value, leaving no separate protocol, submission, and answer labels. The duplicate preflight found no PR for these four checks; [#10045](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10045) covers BFCL training and syntax diagnostics.

**Relevant code**
- [`trial_driver.py#L316-L352`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trial_driver.py#L316-L352) — validates one Harbor dataset and agent.
- [`runner.py#L126-L145`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L126-L145) — reads trial result and trajectory path.
- [`runner.py#L172-L189`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py#L172-L189) — equates reward with `correct`.
- [`eval.py#L111-L141`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finestore/src/finestore/eval.py#L111-L141) — sample and metric contract.
- [`eval.py#L288-L342`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/finestore/src/finestore/eval.py#L288-L342) — flattened trajectory fields.

# Design: agent protocol probes

Add a versioned four-task diagnostic through the evaluation launcher. Pin the model revision, chat template, tool schema/parser, agent/runtime revision, request settings, and task content. Use Harbor's existing local dataset path for sandbox checks; use a dedicated single-turn request to the same served endpoint for `thinking=false`, so the grader can inspect the exact request and response independently of an agent's final message.

1. **Required file.** Ask for a short known answer in `/workspace/answer.txt`. The verifier reads that path in the task environment after the agent stops and records existence, byte count, and content hash. Score file presence separately from matching the known answer; chat text or a claimed write cannot satisfy presence.
2. **Tool execution.** Ask the agent to obtain a per-trial nonce with an exposed shell tool. Record the raw generated response before tool parsing, parsed calls, dispatch/start/end events, and exit status. Label missing or invalid invocation, executor error/timeout, and successful execution separately. A narrated shell session, tool-call markup in ordinary text, or invented tool response must fail the execution check.
3. **Thinking disabled.** Send `enable_thinking=false` only for a pinned template that supports it. Define forbidden reasoning fields and template delimiters for that template; inspect the raw HTTP response and parsed message. An unsupported setting, server error, or extraction failure gets its own status, never a model-violation label. This measures emitted output only.
4. **URL loading.** Supply a task-local HTTP URL serving a per-trial nonce and make a retrieval tool available. Score a request observed by that endpoint or an executor-recorded retrieval attempt. Record no attempt, retrieval/network failure, and successful retrieval separately; compare the answer to the nonce independently. The local endpoint avoids public-site availability as a source of false failures.

Store one versioned evidence bundle per trial with request settings, raw response, parsed calls, execution events, URL access log, and checked file metadata. Archive it alongside the existing raw trajectory through `EvaluationStore`; link it from the sample's grading detail. Export `protocol_compliance`, `submission_completeness`, and `answer_correctness` as distinct numeric metrics; keep `not_evaluable` and its reason in grading detail when a prerequisite failed. Keep `EvalSample.correct` for answer correctness when assessed, and report each rate with its denominator; a structural pass alone cannot raise answer accuracy.

## Validation

Write grader fixtures before implementation. Include positive cases for all four checks: file submission, executed tool call, no emitted reasoning, and successful URL retrieval. Negative cases cover missing and empty files; answer only in chat; a fully narrated fake tool transcript; malformed call; dispatch failure and timeout; URL answer without retrieval and retrieval failure; reasoning-field and delimiter leaks; and a serving/extraction error. Assert both the label and the retained evidence for every fixture. Run the checked-in Harbor config through preflight and one capped end-to-end diagnostic suite covering all four checks on the pinned reference setup before using model comparisons. Keep [#10060](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10060) and [#10061](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10061) separate: they cover general output contracts and tool-call syntax/training.

## Open question

Do the pinned Pi/Harbor/vLLM versions expose the pre-parser generated text and executor lifecycle? The current archive records parsed tool calls and observations, but does not establish those boundaries. If either is unavailable, add capture there before grading that failure class, and mark earlier traces `not_evaluable`.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The [design comment](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10393#issuecomment-6302257478) covers the cause: Harbor maps verifier reward to a single `correct`, and ATIF trajectories record parsed tool calls and observations but no executor lifecycle or pre-parser text. No open PR covers these checks.

- [`runner.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/runner.py) — one reward per trial.
- [`trajectory.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/harbor/trajectory.py) — the trajectory archive the evidence bundle sits beside.
- [`eval.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/3ae74d9560/lib/finestore/src/finestore/eval.py) — `EvalSample`, `Grading.detail`, and `EvaluationStore.add_artifact`.

# Proposed Fix

This PR adds the grader layer in `marin.evaluation.protocol_probes`: a versioned evidence bundle, one typed spec and grader per check, the four minimal tasks, archiving that stores the bundle and links it from the sample, and denominator-aware rates for `protocol_compliance`, `submission_completeness`, and `answer_correctness`. Fixtures cover every positive and negative case listed in the design. When a prerequisite is missing, such as no captured executor lifecycle, the result is `not_evaluable` and never a model violation. A follow-up will connect the tasks to Harbor runs and the served endpoint once the capture question is settled.

issues.author: davidlundgren
issues.body:
Snowball/Grug checkpoints back to the 09.21 Datakit SFT model sometimes write more than one thinking segment in a single assistant message. The usual form is a think block followed by a second segment closed by a stray `<|end_think|>` with no matching `<|start_think|>`. Smartie RL step 14 also stacks complete near-duplicate blocks with nothing between them:

```
<|start_think|>We need to see the files first. Let's list them and examine content.<|end_think|><|start_think|>We need to inspect the files to understand the corrections. Let's list and view them.<|end_think|><|start_think|>We need to see the content. Let's run ls to see files.<|end_think|><|start_think|>I'll list the files in the workspace.<|end_think|>
```

The `grug` reasoning parser moves only the first segment into `reasoning`. It splits at the first `<|start_think|>` and the first `<|end_think|>` ([`basic_parsers.py:157`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/3a054c458ca8a32609ba2bc578c4d9b93eabb395/vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py#L157), inherited by [`grug_reasoning_parser.py`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/3a054c458ca8a32609ba2bc578c4d9b93eabb395/vllm/reasoning/grug_reasoning_parser.py)). Later segments stay in `content` with raw think tags, so users and LLM judges see them. Tool calls after the segments still parse.

The same Smartie conversations also show long thinking-only loops that hit the token limit with an empty reply, for example `\n\nNow.` repeated 7,986 times.

Reproduce:
1. Open case `108de5fc` in the [Smartie step 14 vs Qwen 3.6 comparison](https://applets.marina.oa.dev/a/25f504c6-c6fb-4e14-8401-07dd8e6fbfba/v/28/?run=smartie-rl-step14-vs-qwen36-20261019-v3-final4#108de5fc029a4b65adb39205bdae818e).
2. Round 0, first assistant message: the reply text contains four stacked think blocks before the `ls` tool call.
3. Rounds 2 and 3: the turns end at `finish_reason=length` with no reply.

Expected: at most one think block per assistant message, as rendered by `MARIN_CHAT_TEMPLATE` (`lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py:108`).

Rate by checkpoint on bixbench-pi (eval campaign `eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled`, first 20 tasks per run, final attempt). An assistant message counts when it has two or more thinking segments: a `<|end_think|>` in the text plus a parsed reasoning field, or two or more `<|end_think|>` in raw text.

| Checkpoint | Eval run | Tasks affected | Thinking messages affected |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21 | `20261017-022041-…-bixbench-pi-9e72…` | 6/20 | 19/762 (2.5%) |
| …-2026.09.21-dr-doom | `20261004-053226-…-bixbench-pi-4208` | 8/20 | 16/215 (7.4%) |
| Grug-67B-A2B-Antidoom-RLVR1-Step12-2026.10.02 | `20261003-114254-…-bixbench-pi-ec3e` | 8/20 | 17/279 (6.1%) |
| Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10 | `20261011-111055-…-bixbench-pi-cd7f` | 2/20 | 4/207 (1.9%) |
| Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14 | `20261019-104831-…-bixbench-pi-72d5` | 10/20 | 24/263 (9.1%) |

Run paths are under `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/evals/`; trajectories are `results/harbor_jobs/*/<task>/attempts/*/agent/pi.txt`. In the SFT and Dr. Doom runs, every affected message has exactly two segments. Smartie messages reach five segments.

ShellSim comparison applet, 150 random completed agentic cases per run, counting messages whose parsed `content` or `reasoning` still contains a think tag:

| Checkpoint | Parser | Cases with leftover tags | Messages with leftover tags |
|---|---|---:|---:|
| …-2026.09.21-dr-doom | grug_optional | 0/150 | 0/4,859 |
| Antidoom RLVR1 step 12 | grug_optional | 32/150 | 40/2,148 |
| Antidoom RLVR1 step 12 | grug | 47/150 | 94/2,688 |
| Merge-NUPA-BFCL-Shared100-2026.10.09 | grug | 146/150 | 294/1,757 |
| Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12 | grug | 42/150 | 63/2,699 |
| Smartie RL step 14 | grug | 127/150 | 410/2,666 |
| Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (reference) | qwen3 | 0/150 | 0/2,742 |

`grug_optional` appears to drop stray `<|end_think|>` tags. That hides the two-segment form, so the Dr. Doom zero in the applet does not mean Dr. Doom is clean.

Open questions:
- Source in training data. A sample of 7 rendered SFT sources on `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/rendered/sft/` (nemotron-terminal, agenttrove, openthoughts-agent-sft-100k, gpt-oss-rollouts, glm-5.2-kernelgym-rollouts, coderforge, massive_function_calling; 178k assistant turns) has no turn with more than one think block. These sources are about 10% of the 09.21 SFT tokens. `nemotron_sft_v3` (55%), `open_swe_traces`, and `penfever-traces` were not checked.
- Why the rate rises through RL and merging. Smartie has the highest message rate and the longest stacks; its initializer has the lowest rate in this sample. 20 tasks per checkpoint is a small sample.

Related: #10305 (Smartie RLVR), #9691 (Dr. Doom de-looping).

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported raw generations contain consecutive think blocks; the Smartie step-14 sample has leftover tags in 127/150 cases, versus 0/150 for the Dr. Doom SFT control. The Marin template renders at most one think block per assistant message, while the pinned vLLM parser extracts only the first block, exposing later blocks in `content`. The exact-periodic-suffix loop detector cannot establish whether paraphrased blocks were penalized; the first bad training stage and the proposed FTPO cause remain unverified.

**Relevant code**
- [`chat_template.py#L105-L114`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/036702ca09e1498893582ce1ec6e8e2f04c1bcff/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/chat_template.py#L105-L114) — renders one reasoning span.
- [`basic_parsers.py#L157`](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/3a054c458ca8a32609ba2bc578c4d9b93eabb395/vllm/reasoning/basic_parsers.py#L157) — extracts the first span.
- [`trajectory_reward_shaping.py#L262-L294`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/036702ca09e1498893582ce1ec6e8e2f04c1bcff/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/trajectory_runners/trajectory_reward_shaping.py#L262-L294) — detects exact periodic tails.
- [`ftpo.py#L190-L205`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/036702ca09e1498893582ce1ec6e8e2f04c1bcff/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-train/skyrl_train/ftpo.py#L190-L205) — selects that boundary for FTPO.

# Proposed Fix

1. Run the same fixed ShellSim prompts and generation settings on the Dr. Doom SFT control, the Antidoom step-45 parent if retained, RLVR1 step 12, the Campaign-2 initializer, and Smartie step 14. Save raw token output and parsed messages; report repeated-block, leaked-tag, empty `finish_reason=length`, and task-success rates per checkpoint to locate the first regression.
2. In `marin-community/vllm`, make the Grug reasoning parser consume adjacent balanced think blocks into `reasoning` while preserving reply text and tool calls. Cover full and streaming responses, including incomplete blocks, with parser regression tests; release that serving fix separately.
3. Once the onset is known, inspect the unsampled SFT sources and the responsible training stage, then test a structural training signal for one reasoning span and a completed reply. Re-run the matched cohort before selecting a checkpoint: target 0/150 cases with repeated raw blocks or leaked tags, zero empty length-truncated replies, and no regression in task success. A parser fix alone cannot repair the thinking-only loops.

No open Marin PR matched #10400 or this parser symptom during the duplicate-work check.

🤖 The SFT data does not contain this pattern, so it is not the source.

I scanned the rendered training text behind all 216 stores in the 10.05 SFT mix (`gs://marin-us-central2/grug_sft/stores/full-ab-packed-2026.09.29.json`), reading the first row group of one normalized shard per source:

| | Count |
|---|---|
| Conversations | 593,165 |
| Assistant turns | 2,144,565 |
| Turns with thinking | 1,379,145 |
| Turns with unbalanced think tags | 0 |
| Turns with 2+ think blocks | 23 (0.002%) |

All 23 multi-block turns are in `nemotron_sft_v3/math_v2` (high: 3, low: 20). Each is a short back-to-back pair before a tool call, e.g. `<|start_think|>Compute dot product and magnitudes.<|end_think|><|start_think|>Compute.<|end_think|><tool_call>…`. The stray-end-tag form the models emit never appears.

The 09.21 vs 10.05 SFT comparison rules out even those 23 turns. `math_v2` is only in the 10.05 mix, yet 10.05 leaks less. Fraction of thinking messages with extra segments in the 2026-10-17 eval runs:

| Eval | 09.21 SFT (1,000 steps) | 10.05 SFT (4,750 steps) |
|---|---|---|
| bixbench-pi (20 tasks) | 19/762 (2.5%) | 3/536 (0.6%) |
| bfclparity-pi (40 tasks) | 6/123 (4.9%) | 5/158 (3.2%) |

10.05 shows both forms: `START…END…END` and back-to-back `START…END START…END`.

So the model produces the extra segments itself. The rate falls with longer SFT and rises sharply under RL (Smartie step14: 9.1% of thinking messages on bixbench, up to 5 segments). Fixes belong in the RL stage (reward penalty or rejection of malformed think segments) or in the grug reasoning parser, not in SFT data cleanup.

comments.author: davidlundgren
comments.body:
🤖 The pretraining data teaches the "close, keep reasoning, close again" habit. It comes mostly from one SWE-agent source, `swe-zero-12m`.

### Pretraining scan
I read one row group of normalized shard 0 for every source in the base mixture (`gs://marin-us-central2/datakit/store_8ac06c74`, 114 sources) and counted think tags per document.

- **The pattern:** in about 0.8% of `swe-zero-12m` documents, every assistant turn is `THOUGHT: <reasoning> </thinking>` followed by a bash action, with no opening tag. Some turns close twice or three times: reasoning, `</thinking>`, more reasoning, `</thinking>` again. A second shard gave the same rate (15/1,936 vs 15/1,944 documents).
- **Share of training:** `swe-zero-12m` is about 4% of training tokens and was seen about 4 times. Documents with this shape are about 0.04% of all tokens, roughly 5M stray close tags in total. Over ~10T tokens that is about 5×10⁻⁷ per token (one per ~2M), and about 7% of all think-tag exposure; balanced blocks outnumber it roughly 14:1. It is a single template repeated about 15 times per document, across about 94k SWE-agent transcripts seen about 4 times. So the prior is weak but consistent, and domain-matched to the leaking evals. SFT suppresses it without eliminating it (0.6–2.5%), and RL amplifies it (9%+).
- **Bare `</think>`:** `davinci-dev/env-native` has `</think>` with no opening tag in 3% of its documents. It is only 0.07% of the mixture.
- **Clean sources:** the multi-turn reasoning sources (nemotron-terminal, the nemotron SFT sets, gpt-oss-rollouts) have one balanced think block per turn. General web text has no tags.
- **Phases:** pretraining, cooldown and the step-156k→157k context extension that the SFT started from all draw from this one store. Only the bucket weights change between phases, so this data is present right up to the base checkpoint.

The base checkpoint (`open-athena/snowball-67b-a2b-base-262k-qk175-skew8`) shows the same shape. In its SWE-bench eval it emitted plain-text `</think>` 6,546 times and `<think>` 307 times across 595 agent messages.

The base model writes these as plain-text tags, while SFT and RL models use the `<|end_think|>` special token, so the habit has to carry over across forms. That is plausible but not shown. A few-shot base test is running to measure it.

### Rendering parity: ruled out
For the main eval path (pi agent, `reasoning_parser: null`, hermes tools), the inference prompt matches the SFT rendering token for token, in simulated and real bixbench trajectories. The model also leaks on turn 0, before it has any history. The grug parser with streaming does garble history once a leak exists: `extract_reasoning_streaming` drops lone think tokens. That is a secondary bug, not the cause.

### RL amplifies it
The answer extractor (`final_answer_text`) keeps the text after the last close marker, and SWE grading parses tool calls across the whole completion. Multi-segment completions therefore get full reward. Nothing pushes back once RL samples the pattern.

### Examples
<details><summary>swe-zero-12m: no opening tag, one close per turn (doc 0069b90849b08e72)</summary>

~~~
<assistant>
THOUGHT: … 4. The subject validation regex needs to be updated to match the new requirements

Let me examine the exact function that needs fixing and also check the validateSubject function.
</thinking>

Let me look at the specific functions mentioned in the issue:

```bash
grep -n "StreamNameBySubject\|validateSubject" ./jetstream/jetstream.go
```
</assistant>
~~~
</details>

<details><summary>swe-zero-12m: three closes in one turn (doc 0b9c2b7c6e98e2f6, turn 12)</summary>

~~~
THOUGHT: Now I need to understand the problem better. …
I think the real issue is in how we determine what proxy counts should be used. Let me examine the current logic more systematically.
</thinking>

Looking at the issue description and the code I can see, I believe the problem is in the `GetRoleCountsWithDefaults` function. … [~1.4k chars of further reasoning]
Let me implement a fix that addresses the core issue:
</thinking>

Let me first check if there are any imports or dependencies I need to understand better.
</thinking>

```bash
grep -n "import\|Version\|VersionFlags" ./api/v1beta2/foundationdb_database_configuration.go | head -20
```
~~~
</details>

<details><summary>davinci-dev/env-native: bare close at the start of a turn</summary>

~~~
<assistant>
I'll help you implement… 探寻代码仓库结构，找到与 literally 和内联函数相关的代码。</think>
I'll help you fix the issue… <tool_call:bash> …
~~~
</details>

<details><summary>For contrast, SFT math_v2/high: back-to-back blocks (one of the 23 SFT turns)</summary>

~~~
<|start_think|>We cannot use python now. It seems Python environment is dead. … Let's try again but perhaps with a simpler "Run code" approach.<|end_think|><|start_think|>We can attempt to reinitialize the python tool. … Alternative: We can do analysis manually …
~~~
</details>
