comments.body:
🤖 Few-shot base test results (follow-up to "a few-shot base test is running" above).

Each run used 200 raw-completion prompts with four plain-text `<think>…</think>\nAnswer:` examples, each containing exactly one think block. Rows below count completions that close, keep going, and close again:

| Model | T=1.0 (n=400) | T=0.6 (n=400) | greedy (n=200) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Base, step 157k | 12 (3.0%, CI 1.7–5.2%) | 0 | 0 |
| 10.05 SFT | 6 (1.5%, CI 0.7–3.2%) | 0 | 0 |

The base model already has a weak "close, then continue" tail, and it shows up only at high temperature. SFT reduces it, though the confidence intervals overlap. RL rollouts sample at high temperature and the graders reward the pattern, which fits the amplification seen under RL. Some base-model cases are plain run-on continuation, not resumed reasoning. Plain-text tags are not the `<|end_think|>` token, so these rates don't compare directly with the eval rates.

Cheap follow-up: rerun bixbench-pi and bfclparity-pi at T=0.6 to check whether the leak disappears.

comments.author: XiaoyuanWang111
comments.body:
🤖 In the evaluation campaign's Evalchemy runs, the issue's two-segment form reaches the graders as answer text. The `eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled` Grug model configs set no reasoning parser and no `skip_special_tokens` ([step 14's](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/model-configs/open-athena-Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14.yaml#L10-L22)), so vLLM's default `skip_special_tokens: true` deletes `<|start_think|>` and `<|end_think|>` (special tokens [128002 and 128003](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/experiments/marin_tokenizer.py#L30-L31)) and Evalchemy receives the stray reasoning and the answer as one text. The `snowball-sft` entry keeps them with `skip_special_tokens: "false"` ([models.py#L129-L137](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/experiments/evaluation/models.py#L129-L137)).

The fix is commit [f50d536](https://github.com/XiaoyuanWang111/marin/commit/f50d536116e6bb7c5bc693a461179de716e709fe) on the `campaign-grug-keep-think-tokens` branch of XiaoyuanWang111/marin, based on main 80efd705e; it merges cleanly into main 41a41987e. It sets `generation.extra_gen_kwargs.skip_special_tokens: "false"` in the 25 Grug and Snowball configs Evalchemy runs read: the 24 in `model-configs/` and the TriviaQA override. Harbor runs do not read that field ([model_config.py#L167-L168](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/model_config.py#L167-L168)), so this issue's agent runs and the Harbor-only `tau3/` overrides are unaffected; the structure-closure script already sends `skip_special_tokens: False`.

The [`grug` reasoning parser](https://github.com/marin-community/vllm/blob/01911be34fac8715347962a8d791ca34a879e01e/vllm/reasoning/grug_reasoning_parser.py#L43-L54) in Marin's GPU vLLM pin (01911be3, marin-community/vllm#79) would also keep the markers, but it splits each reply at its first `<|start_think|>` and first `<|end_think|>`, as the issue describes, and Evalchemy's default `combine` puts the first segment back in front of the rest without a marker ([completion_response.py#L70-L71](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/completion_response.py#L70-L71)). MMLU-Pro, MATH500 and AIME24 read the final content first ([mmlu.py#L12-L19](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/graders/mmlu.py#L12-L19), [answer_extraction.py#L50-L57](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/graders/answer_extraction.py#L50-L57)) and would get the text after the first `<|end_think|>`, but IFBench would still check the stray reasoning, and NUPA5K-Loose's cut after the last `<|end_think|>` would find no marker between the reasoning and the answer. We have not run the parser.

We sampled the campaign's eight thinking-off generation benchmarks once per prompt for `Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14` (step 14, Snowball v0.1), `Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign2-DARE-TIES-02-2026.10.10` (Campaign2), `Grug-67B-A2B-Datakit-SFT-262K-2026.09.21` (SFT 09.21), `Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.17.49-step12` (.49 step 12, the tournament's second place) and `Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.19.57-step8` (.57 step 8). We sent the campaign's requests plus `skip_special_tokens: false` and graded each reply with the markers deleted, as the campaign's graders get it, and with them kept. The requests set `enable_thinking: false` ([ifbench.yaml#L13-L14](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/evalchemy-configs/ifbench.yaml#L13-L14)) and no temperature ([robust_api.py#L182-L185](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/robust_api.py#L182-L185)), and the five checkpoints' `generation_config.json` set none ([step 14's](https://huggingface.co/open-athena/Snowball-Smartie-RL-2026.10.15.32-step14/blob/6783e9743478bd25a9ce03ab3460e84d6a9814b0/generation_config.json)), so they sample at 1.0, where your few-shot test found the "close, then continue" tail. Replies with a generated `<|end_think|>`:

| Benchmark (prompts) | Step 14 | Campaign2 | SFT 09.21 | .49 step 12 | .57 step 8 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| TriviaQA (17,944) | 1,374 | 306 | 158 | 1,948 | 213 |
| CRUXEval (1,600) | 328 | 63 | 90 | 802 | 890 |
| MBPP+ (378) | 376 | 3 | 0 | 10 | 334 |
| HumanEval+ (164) | 163 | 1 | 0 | 3 | 53 |
| GSM8K 0-shot (1,319) | 28 | 3 | 1 | 5 | 44 |
| MRCR (1,196) | 19 | 9 | 3 | 8 | 20 |
| IFBench (300) | 26 | 6 | 2 | 40 | 16 |
| FinanceBench (50) | 4 | 0 | 0 | 4 | 3 |

Step 14's MBPP+ and HumanEval+ replies also hold a generated `<|start_think|>` (376 of 378 and 162 of 164), and so do 342, 63 and 1,355 of .57 step 8's MBPP+, HumanEval+ and CRUXEval replies.

Keeping the markers moves almost none of these scores, because most of these graders read the whole reply ([IFBench's](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/graders/instructions.py#L23)). IFBench, GSM8K (also under #10808's scorer), HumanEval+, MBPP+, CRUXEval and FinanceBench (gpt-oss-120b judge; campaign launches since #10655 use [MiniMax-M3](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/experiments/evaluation/campaigns/eval-campaign-09-25-unlabeled/README.md#L40-L41)) do not change on any checkpoint. TriviaQA loses 6, 4, 2 and 1 of 17,944 replies on step 14, SFT 09.21, .49 step 12 and .57 step 8, and none on Campaign2. MRCR's accuracy falls by at most 0.009 points (step 14: 21.612 to 21.603), and one step-14 reply loses its prefix hit (`prefix_hit_rate`). In an earlier step-14 IFBench_test sample (temperature 1.0, our own client, `max_tokens` 32,768), grading only the text after the last `<|end_think|>` raised strict prompt-level accuracy from 29.7% to 31.7% (6 prompts gained, none lost; exact McNemar p = 0.031). Greedy decoding without a repetition penalty left a generated `<|end_think|>` in 7 of those 300 replies, against 25 at 1.0, and the cut changed no grade.

The campaign runs MMLU-Pro, AIME24, MATH500 and NUPA5K-Loose with thinking on, and they already grade only the text after the last `<|end_think|>`. Sampled the same way, MATH500 moves by 0 to +0.6 points, NUPA5K-Loose by +42 to +67 on all five checkpoints under main's [scorer](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/chat_benchmarks/NUPA-Loose/scorer.py#L56-L59) and by +0.3 to +4.6 on four of them under [marin-community/evalchemy@2baaab1b](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/commit/2baaab1b9c0c9c8caffcd8f6df45355539aef436) (branch `benfeuer/eval-policy-09-25-draft`), the scorer of the campaign's NUPA replay, and MMLU-Pro by +0.9 to +6.4, because without the marker its extractor takes the first case-insensitive `answer is` match in the whole reply. Of the five checkpoints' 1,500 AIME24 replies, 3 are right only with the markers kept and none only without them, and none of their 1,500 OlympiadBench replies changes grade. GPQA Diamond, whose [grader](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/graders/math_specs.py#L57-L63) reads the whole reply, was not measured. The exception is .57 step 8 under `2baaab1b`, which loses 6.8 points: 639 of its 5,000 NUPA5K-Loose replies open a think block again after their last `<|end_think|>` and stop inside it, and with the markers kept the scorer finds no final answer in 363 replies it credits with them deleted, 270 of them reopened. The same pattern shows in 9,670 of its 12,032 MMLU-Pro replies, but MMLU-Pro's grader reads everything after the last `<|end_think|>`, still finds an answer in 9,517 of them, and the kept markers add 0.9 points.

To grade only the final answer, the thinking-off graders other than GSM8K's boxed answers (since #10808) would also need the [`final_response_text`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/f4b7d5ace57acef1dde9234214a58764ed1f0138/vendor/evalchemy/eval/graders/answer_extraction.py#L39-L45) cut. The evaluation driver in #10757 has no field for `skip_special_tokens` ([`generation_options`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9fcf9f6f4a792e0f6b6b5dafa9c10353818ceadc/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/task_driver.py#L130-L151), [`ChatModel`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/9fcf9f6f4a792e0f6b6b5dafa9c10353818ceadc/experiments/evaluation/task_driver.py#L85)), so Grug runs through it would need one to keep the markers.

Method: the GPU release of marin-community/vllm@e09cfd55 (CUDA 12.9; our pod cannot run the pinned 01911be3's CUDA 13.2 build) on four H100s, data parallel 4 with expert parallelism, without the configs' weight-loading flag `--model-loader-extra-config '{"distributed":true}'`; requests built and sent by Marin's Evalchemy at 80efd705e from the campaign's client configs. The markers-deleted text was rebuilt from each reply's token ids with vLLM's detokenizer and `skip_special_tokens: true`, and Evalchemy graded both texts.

Each step is scored by teacher forcing on a fixed set of 10.05 trajectories. Runs are in the W&B project `marin_moe_sft`; the harness code is on #10851 (closed, not merged). **What the hazard plots measure.** 10.05 sampled reasoning up to its first `<|end_think|>`, then 256 more tokens. "No lead-in" means nothing was inserted after the close; "lead-in" means a phrase like "Wait," was forced in. Hazard = 1 − ∏(1 − p(`<|end_think|>`)) over those 256 tokens: the chance of a second close if the model wrote exactly what 10.05 wrote. It's scored on 10.05's text, so it's off-policy for every other checkpoint, and it's not a sampled rate. **No lead-in: peak (step) → step 100** | | " answer" init (`replay-10400-base300e`) | mean-row init (`replay-10400-meanseed`) | 10.05 | 09.21* | |---|---|---|---|---| | SWE | 0.136 (19) → 0.017 | 0.069 (59) → 0.030 | 0.0008 | 0.004 | | tool-using | 0.223 (15) → 0.019 | 0.014 (60) → 0.011 | 0.0065 | 0.0048 | | plain | 0.075 (13) → 0.002 | 0.002 → 0.002 | 0.0001 | 0.0006 | \*09.21 comes from vLLM top-20 logprobs, so it's a lower bound. At the peak, roughly 1 SWE turn in 7 would close twice; for 10.05 it's about 1 in 1,250. As a sanity check, 10.05's sampled no-lead-in re-close rate on the same prompts was 0/109 for SWE and 5/197 for tool-using, the same order as its hazard. **After a lead-in: step 100** | | " answer" init | mean-row init | 10.05 | 09.21* | |---|---|---|---|---| | SWE | 0.58 | 0.68 | 0.35 | 0.47 | | tool-using | 0.31 | 0.30 | 0.21 | 0.17 | | plain | 0.085 | 0.091 | 0.054 | 0.062 | **1. Init of the `<|end_think|>` row.** Initializing the row from the mean of the other rows, instead of from " answer", delays learning by ~40 steps. Both runs land at the same after-lead-in hazard. The big early no-lead-in spike is mostly an " answer"-init effect: with the mean-row init, only SWE spikes. **2. Training only the `<|end_think|>` row on the frozen base (`replay-10400-closerow`, cancelled at step 32).** This was meant to test whether the habit already lives in the pretrained features. It learns far too slowly to say: ~10× every 25 steps versus every 6 for the full run, ending around 1e-6. There's a weak hint the base features already favor re-close positions (~2× over the real close, 4–8× after a lead-in). Most of the full run's early learning comes from the rest of the network adapting. A close row fit to convergence on frozen base hidden states would settle this; not run. **3. What the failures in the wild look like.** I classified every assistant message with more than one think segment in two bixbench-pi runs per checkpoint (~440 tasks each). | | 09.21 | 10.05 | |---|---|---| | messages with thinking | 6,182 | 15,232 | | messages with an extra segment | 138 (2.2%) | 54 (0.35%) | | reasoning, close, X, close again | 134 | 35 | | …followed by a tool call | 115 | 33 | | X is findings/explanation prose | 101 | 25 | | X is next-step narration ("Now let me…") | 32 | 10 | | X starts with a lead-in ("Wait", "Actually") | 1 | 0 | Typical: `…<|end_think|>Now let me run the final solution …<|end_think|>`. This "prose → close tag → action" shape is the `swe-zero-12m` pattern from the pretraining scan above, which keeps pretraining a live suspect. The lead-in hazard measures a related situation, not this one. **4. A metric that tracks the real failure.** p(`<|end_think|>`) at the end of the visible prose, right before the tool call, teacher-forced on 768 reconstructed bixbench sessions (turns before pi's 32K compaction only): | checkpoint | turns 10.05 wrote (236) | turns 09.21 wrote (738) | |---|---|---| | replay step 100 (mean-row init) | 0.15 | 0.10 | | 09.21 | 0.095 | 0.035 | | 10.05 | 0.013 | 0.008 | It ranks 09.21 above 10.05, matching their failure rates in the wild (2.2% vs 0.35%). The base model can't be scored this way, because the `<|end_think|>` row is freshly reset before SFT. **Open** * a sampled stray-close rate and the end-of-prose metric per step. The replay checkpoints have expired, so this needs a rerun that saves checkpoints. * pretraining vs SFT: fit the `<|end_think|>` row to convergence on frozen base features. * #10850 already showed the #10519 renderer fix doesn't change the hazard in the first 50 steps.

comments.body:
🤖 Correction to the [pretraining scan](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6327348899): counted per tag, the 23 sources it scanned contribute about 36.6M balanced think blocks and 5.4M stray closes (close tags with no opening tag) over the ~10T-token run, a ratio of about 7:1. The scan's 14:1 compares token shares: 0.56% of training tokens are in documents with balanced think tags, and 0.04% are in documents with stray closes. Per tag, stray closes are 13% of close tags and 7% of all open and close tags.

`<think>` has 34.92M balanced blocks and 0.01M stray closes. `<thinking>` has 1.64M balanced blocks, all in gpt-oss-rollouts, and 5.42M stray closes, all in swe-zero-12m.

27M of the balanced blocks come from math, code and chat data: nemotron_sft math, code and general, and infinibyte_reasoning. The [latest analysis](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10400#issuecomment-6589737235) found that most bixbench-pi failures are turns that close their visible prose with `<|end_think|>` right before a tool call. In the agent-transcript sources, which log a model reasoning, running commands and reading their output over many turns, the ratio is 1.7:1 and 37% of close tags are stray:

| Agent-transcript source | Balanced blocks | Stray closes |
|---|---|---|
| nemotron-terminal | 7.7M `<think>` | ~0 (1 tag in the sample) |
| gpt-oss-rollouts | 1.6M `<thinking>` | 0 |
| swe-zero-12m | 0 | 5.4M `</thinking>` |
| davinci-dev/env-native | 0 | 0.008M `</think>` |
| Total | 9.3M | 5.4M |

swe-rebench-openhands and coderforge are also agent transcripts and have no think tags in the sample.

These counts measure exposure to each pattern. They do not show that the base model learned the habit from this data. The open frozen-feature test in the latest analysis checks whether the base model already has the habit before SFT.

Method and limits:
- Each scanned source contributes one row group of normalized shard 0. Its counts are scaled to its training tokens, which are estimated from the buckets its shard-0 documents fall in and each phase's bucket weights. Phase 0 covers 8.05T tokens (steps 0 to 127.5k) and phase 1 covers 1.98T (the rest of the run, including the cooldown and context extension).
- The scan comment says it read every source in the mixture. It read 23 of the 114 sources, which hold about 2.9T of the training tokens. A second sample drew 208k documents by bucket weight from 167 of the store's 200 buckets, so it includes unread sources. It gives 35.6M balanced blocks, consistent with the unread sources adding few tags. Only 68 of its documents contain think tags, so this is a rough check, and it is too small to measure the swe-zero-12m pattern.
- These are plain-text tags. SFT and RL use the `<|start_think|>` and `<|end_think|>` special tokens.

issues.author: penfever
issues.body:
## TL;DR

Build and validate an instruction-following benchmark whose checks implement the stated instructions and distinguish formatting compliance from answer quality. The [localized FTPO campaign #10043](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043) found real instruction failures alongside checker weaknesses in IFBench. Keep its official scores in the record; do not remove cases because a preferred model fails them.

## Description

The Recovery baseline scored 82/300 on IFBench loose-prompt accuracy. Runs `2026.10.12.2`, `.3`, and `.4` scored 78, 79, and 84. Strict accuracy for `.2` and `.3` was 68/300 versus baseline 73/300. Loose normalizes some formatting differences but does not fix the underlying constraint validators. These observations do not establish general instruction-following regression or preservation.

The trace audit used [Evalchemy `97fffeb`](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/tree/97fffeb7df60875c5a5c14ec215dd4e7683102c5), specifically [grader.py](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/97fffeb7df60875c5a5c14ec215dd4e7683102c5/eval/chat_benchmarks/IFBench/grader.py) and [instructions.py](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/97fffeb7df60875c5a5c14ec215dd4e7683102c5/eval/chat_benchmarks/IFBench/instructions.py). The public campaign report and result tracker contain measured scores; trace archives remain access-controlled.

The numeric IDs below are evaluator `doc_id` values in the retained `allenai/IFBench_test` records, not asserted universal dataset IDs. The evaluator loaded the dataset without an explicit Hub revision; no immutable upstream dataset revision is asserted. Exact prompt comparisons were made against the retained evaluation artifacts. A replacement must pin both data and checker versions.

Observed issues to turn into regression fixtures:

- List-marker tasks 83/84: the checker counts the special marker anywhere, although its description requires line starts. Missing or altered `!?!?` markers are also genuine failures and must remain failures.
- Nested-bracket tasks 106/111: accumulated depth can satisfy the checker without a fully balanced structure. In task 106 a disordered 197,987-character baseline response passed, while a 2,144-character candidate response answering the math question failed the structural condition. Semantic usefulness and structural compliance need separate scores.
- Quotation tasks 115/117 and 123/124: quote adjacency, nesting, and whitespace handling can interact with explanatory text. Define the exact accepted language and validate it with independent fixtures.
- HTML task 138: one italic region plus text can pass without satisfying the requested coverage of sections.
- Palindrome task 234: occurrence counting can reward repetition rather than distinct qualifying words; the baseline passed with 50 repeated occurrences.
- Stopword task 176: the Recovery response had 5,576 characters; run `2026.10.12.3` passed with 289,654 characters. Constraint satisfaction alone does not capture usefulness, repetition, or bounded completion.
- Option-only tasks 100/103: duplicated options or added explanation violate the instruction. These are positive controls for genuine model failure, not benchmark defects.

The `.3` model had 12 strict losses and seven gains relative to baseline; 11 of the losses involved formatting constraints. Eight losses were shared with `.2`. Responses over 100,000 characters fell from 50 at baseline to 13 in `.2` and 20 in `.3`, so a uniform verbosity increase does not explain the results. Stored responses contain reasoning-like prose, but the audit did not independently prove a reasoning-channel extraction bug.

## Hypothesis or goal

A benchmark with explicit output contracts, independently tested validators, and separate semantic/format measures will better detect useful instruction-following changes than a single aggregate pass rate over weak constraints.

## Status and proposed experiment

Proposed; no new data collection or training is launched by this issue.

1. Specify whether each instruction applies to final-answer content, the whole visible response, or structured output. Test reasoning/final-channel extraction independently. Do not silently strip content to improve a model's score.
2. Publish a versioned taxonomy covering exact choice, counts, ordering, formatting, structured outputs, multi-constraint composition, and semantic requirements. Define ambiguous instructions before collecting labels.
3. Build validator fixtures with valid alternative answers, near misses, malformed structures, repeated garbage, quoted markers, and adversarial counterexamples. Use metamorphic tests: changes irrelevant to an instruction should preserve its label. Cross-check structural validators with an independent implementation.
4. Report semantic task correctness separately from literal contract compliance. Measure output length, repetition, truncation, extraction failures, and infrastructure coverage. A short answer is not automatically correct; a long answer is not automatically incorrect.
5. Split by task/template family before generating variants. Reserve new held-out compositions and constraint combinations. Do not tune validators or choose examples against only the released FTPO checkpoint.
6. Evaluate Recovery, the released Protocol-FTPO model, and diverse comparison models under fixed serving settings and matched budgets. Repeat generations, publish paired uncertainty estimates, and predeclare acceptable regression margins. Retain official IFBench Strict and Loose as reference panels.

Done when the dataset, validator source, adversarial fixtures, versioned protocol, and model comparison are published with provenance and redistribution clearance; observed IFBench defects have reproducible fixtures; and the report distinguishes corrected measurement from changed model ability. If the replacement is not more reliable, report that result.

## Links

- Parent experiment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043
- Related protocol-composition experiment: https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10061
- Public campaign evidence: https://huggingface.co/datasets/open-athena/BFCL-Protocol-FTPO-Results/tree/a7bbbfbe05e16ee5cadbbcdd8135fbf59b40cfb7

## Decision log

The parent campaign changed its primary IF metric to Loose after inspecting traces. This follow-up keeps both official scores and tests a replacement without retroactively relabeling the parent results.

## Conclusion

Pending benchmark validation and comparative evaluation.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The [FTPO campaign](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10043) measured 82/300 IFBench Loose for Recovery and 78/300 for the selected checkpoint, but the audit in this issue found checker defects alongside genuine constraint failures. Marin pins Evalchemy at `d1a1005` and currently excludes IFBench from its working chat-task catalog; its served runner can already launch file-backed tasks and preserve per-sample outputs. No open Marin PR matched #10060 or IFBench during the duplicate-work check; [#10061](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10061) covers tool-call skill training, while this issue owns instruction-following measurement.

**Relevant code**

- [Evalchemy pin](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/external_dependencies.py#L55-L62) — runtime revision.
- [Chat task catalog](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/evaluation/evals.py#L295-L298) — IFBench exclusion.
- [File-backed launch path](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/experiments/evaluation/README.md#L110-L137) — configuration and provenance.
- [Sample archive adapter](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/lm_eval_samples.py#L1-L10) — retained per-case evidence.
- [Original checker](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/blob/97fffeb7df60875c5a5c14ec215dd4e7683102c5/eval/chat_benchmarks/IFBench/instructions.py) — audited contract implementation.

# Proposed Fix

**Design.** Add a versioned instruction-following task to the Evalchemy fork and run it through Marin's existing file-backed evaluation path. Keep official IFBench Strict and Loose results as an unchanged reference panel. The new task will score the stated output contract and answer quality separately, with explicit extraction and coverage outcomes, so a validator correction cannot be presented as a change in model ability.

**Contract and data.** Publish a protocol manifest that pins the source dataset revision and row hashes, checker source commit, extraction rule, prompt/template version, split assignment, serving settings, and metric definitions. Each case declares whether its constraints cover final-answer text, the whole visible response, or a structured payload. A sample record carries the raw response, extracted text or extraction failure, per-constraint labels, a semantic label or not-applicable status, output length, repetition, truncation, and an infrastructure status. A run with missing expected samples fails coverage validation; infrastructure failures are reported separately from model accuracy. Define ambiguous instructions before labels are collected; keep adjudications and rationale in the versioned protocol.

**Validation.** First replay the retained 300-case prompts and responses through Evalchemy `97fffeb` and confirm the recorded Strict/Loose values before changing a checker. Then build synthetic, redistributable positive and negative fixtures for the observed list-marker (83/84), bracket (106/111), quotation (115/117/123/124), HTML (138), palindrome (234), stopword (176), and option-only (100/103) cases. Include valid alternate answers, malformed structures, quoted markers, repetition, and irrelevant-text transformations. Cross-check bracket and structured-output labels with an independent parser; use blinded human adjudication for semantic labels and checker disagreements. Case numbers are retained evaluator `doc_id` values; fixture identity will instead use a stable content hash plus task-family ID.

**Holdout and comparison.** Freeze taxonomy and task-family split before generating variants; reserve unseen templates and constraint compositions for the held-out panel. Run Recovery, the released Protocol-FTPO checkpoint, and at least two distinct comparison models with the same prompt rendering, decoding budgets, extraction rule, and repeated-generation schedule. Predeclare the primary contract and semantic metrics, regression margins, and family-clustered paired uncertainty method before viewing the new panel's model results. Report official Strict/Loose beside corrected contract and semantic scores, per-family denominators, extraction and infrastructure failures, length, repetition, and truncation. A correct short answer and a useful long answer remain eligible under their stated contracts.

**Delivery sequence.** (1) Freeze the manifest, output-surface rules, fixtures, and adjudication guide; check whether [Evalchemy PR #23](https://github.com/marin-community/evalchemy/pull/23) can be extended before opening fork work. (2) Land the task and fixture suite in Evalchemy, with complete requested-task/sample coverage as a success condition. (3) Pin the validated fork revision, add a Marin Evalchemy YAML, and verify a bounded served smoke run writes the promised per-sample fields and metrics. (4) Freeze the held-out panel, run the matched comparison, and publish the dataset, validator source, protocol, aggregate and per-family results, and negative findings where allowed. Confirm redistribution rights before releasing retained prompts or responses; synthetic fixtures can be public independently. No training run is part of this issue.

**Decision gate.** Call the replacement more reliable only if the adversarial fixtures and independent checks pass, scored-case coverage is complete, and blinded review finds fewer contract-label errors than the frozen checker on a preselected audit sample. Report the comparison even if that gate fails. The remaining design decision is the exact semantic annotation rubric and agreement threshold; record both before model outputs from the held-out panel are inspected.

spillover_issues.author: penfever
spillover_issues.body:
We believe that formal verification is essential for open source models to get better at math, and better generally! Lean, a popular formal verification language primarily used for mathematical proofs, is one of the most popular avenues for this kind of improvement. We don't have RL data we trust for Lean, nor do we have evals we trust. Marin needs both in order to continue improving in this domain.

cc @Robertboy18

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

Marin already grades Nemotron RLVR1 Lean responses with a pinned Lean 4.12/Mathlib compiler ([#10080](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10080), [#10088](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10088)). That establishes a reward path for those rows, but not an audited training corpus or held-out theorem-proving eval. [#10214](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10214) excluded Lean from its mixed RLVR runs because Iris task pods could not start the Docker task machine; the [current eval policy](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10197) lists no Lean proof benchmark.

**Relevant code**
- [lean_grade.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/lean_grade.py) — current compiler-backed reward.
- [lean.Dockerfile](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/post_training/task_curation/datasets/nemotron_ultra/lean.Dockerfile) — pinned toolchain and Mathlib.
- [lean_compiler.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/vendor/skyrl/skyrl-gym/skyrl_gym/lean_compiler.py) — task-local execution path.
- [proofpile.py](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/main/experiments/datasets/proofpile.py) — existing pretraining corpus to check for overlap.

# Proposed Fix

1. **Freeze the eval first.** Inventory candidate Lean problem sets and record licenses, source revisions, theorem IDs, proof provenance, and required toolchains. Create public development and sealed test manifests; check statement/proof overlap against RLVR1, Proof-Pile 2, and proposed training sources. Specify prompts, token and time budgets, pass@1/pass@k, and how compiler failures and missing scores enter the denominator. Done when pinned reruns reproduce the same task IDs and verdicts.
2. **Audit the verifier.** Reuse the compiler path with controls for invalid proofs, `sorry`/`admit`, changed statements, extra axioms, and timeouts. Review a stratified sample of accepted and rejected attempts independently, publish disagreement counts, and resolve reward exploits before training. Keep the compiler and Mathlib revision identical between data validation and eval.
3. **Curate RL tasks.** Normalize licensed Lean statements and headers into provenance-bearing task records, deduplicate by theorem and near-duplicate text, and compile reference proofs where provided. Keep eval problems and their proof variants out of training. Resolve the Iris task-pod execution gap seen in #10214, then run a real task-session smoke test. Done when each released row has a source, toolchain pin, verification outcome, and contamination decision.
4. **Measure transfer.** Run pinned baseline models on the frozen eval, reporting pass@1/pass@k with uncertainty, per-source scores, and compiler/error rates. Compare a small Lean RL pilot against its starting checkpoint on the same eval and publish the dataset and run revisions. Expand the data or training budget only if the audited reward and held-out scores support it.

comments.body:
Thanks! I looked through what's out there, and a few things seem worth starting from:

- **One Lean version for data and evals.** I'd suggest v4.34.1: it has the fix for a kernel bug that allowed an axiom-free proof of `False` (leanprover/lean4#14576), and it's what Prime Intellect's Lean environments and openai/math use.
- **Evals:** [PutnamBench](https://github.com/trishullab/PutnamBench), [miniF2F (DeepMind fork)](https://github.com/google-deepmind/miniF2F) and [ProofNet-Verified](https://github.com/marcusm117/ProofNet-Verified), with [Lean Eval](https://github.com/leanprover/lean-eval) as a hard ceiling.
- **RL data:** [Goedel RL_dataset_V2](https://huggingface.co/datasets/Goedel-LM/RL_dataset_V2), [NuminaMath-LEAN](https://huggingface.co/datasets/project-numina/NuminaMath-LEAN) and [Kimina](https://huggingface.co/datasets/project-numina/Kimina-Prover-Promptset), plus [mathlib-tactics](https://huggingface.co/datasets/mathlib-initiative/mathlib-tactics) for SFT warm-up.
- **Environments:** [Prime's Lean environments](https://github.com/PrimeIntellect-ai/prime-envs/tree/main/environments/lean) have the strictest grader I found and already filter these datasets for v4.34. Their env code only runs on Prime's VMs, but the image and checker are Apache-2.0, so we could reuse them in Harbor. [FineEnvs/openai-math](https://huggingface.co/datasets/FineEnvs/openai-math) runs on Harbor today.

One gap: nobody has the code-verification benchmarks (VERINA, CLEVER, Vericoding, FVSpec) on one version yet. I have them internally and will make them public once I've upgraded them all to v4.34.1. Which track would you like first?

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
Add a way to run small evaluations and generation jobs against OpenRouter free models, with coordination on an Iris CPU task and inference hosted by OpenRouter. The free tier is useful for a pilot, but its daily request cap makes it unsuitable for high-volume generation without further capacity planning.

OpenRouter documents 20 requests/minute and 50 requests/day for free variants, or 1,000/day after qualifying credit purchases. Failed attempts count; keys and cluster replicas do not multiply the shared capacity. The actual account quota and provider availability still need verification. At 50/day, a 500-example, one-call evaluation takes at least 10 days. See [free models and limits](https://openrouter.ai/collections/free-models) and [quota/error details](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits).

On October 31, 2026, the [model catalog](https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/models) listed 16 named `:free` chat models and `openrouter/free`. Initial candidates, based on advertised capabilities rather than measured quality:

| Model | Pilot use | Advertised context |
| --- | --- | ---: |
| `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning:free` | Text and tools | 1,000,000 |
| `nvidia/nemotron-3.5-super-vl:free` | Vision and structured output | 1,000,000 |
| `cohere/north-mini-code:free` | Coding | 256,000 |

The catalog changes, and provider availability and actual capabilities must be checked at runtime. [`openrouter/free`](https://openrouter.ai/docs/guides/routing/routers/free-router) randomly chooses a qualifying model, so pin model IDs and record the returned model/provider for comparable evaluations.

A first implementation could run one CPU-only Iris coordinator with outbound HTTPS and bounded concurrency. The coordinator reads a task manifest, admits requests against a shared account quota, sends OpenAI-compatible chat requests to `https://openrouter.ai/api/v1`, and stores results and attempt metadata in available same-region storage. Start with a conservative 15 requests/minute and concurrency 2, and query `GET /api/v1/key` for `free_model_daily_requests`. Reconcile a shared quota across all clients and model IDs; honor `Retry-After`, stop on configuration or authentication errors, and pause until the daily quota resets when exhausted. Account-specific quota and behavior remain to be tested.

Use a free-model allowlist, prohibit paid fallbacks and plugins, and consider a zero `provider.max_price` filter as an additional guard. Load the OpenRouter API key inside the coordinator using an appropriate cluster secret mechanism; do not expose it to clients or logs. Record request ID, requested and returned model, parameters, attempt count, output, usage, latency, and errors. Resume from committed results after restart. A timed-out request may already have completed upstream, so retrying it can consume quota again. Check data retention and model/provider terms before sending nonpublic inputs or using outputs for training; the [NVIDIA free endpoint terms](https://openrouter.ai/nvidia/nemotron-3.5-lightning%3Afree/) specifically prohibit confidential or personal inputs and describe logging.

The existing inference interfaces are useful starting points ([endpoint-oriented evaluation #4827](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4827#issuecomment-4262089762), [centralized Iris inference RFC #4401](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4401)). An external-provider path needs to address these current constraints:

- [`IrisConfig`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ef434a11a548d0df04a0be801267ac03031184c0/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/config.py#L429) rejects CPU inference workers; an external API worker should not require an accelerator.
- [`InferenceWorker`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ef434a11a548d0df04a0be801267ac03031184c0/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/worker.py#L180) forwards caller headers and does not apply `OpenAIEndpoint.api_key`; an upstream worker needs to inject its own credential and validate its allowed models.
- The broker queue is in memory. Shared quota admission and resumable results need durable state. [`OpenAIChatClient`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/ef434a11a548d0df04a0be801267ac03031184c0/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/openai_chat.py) reduces HTTP failures to `ConnectionError`, so callers cannot use structured status and response headers for retry decisions.

Done when:

- A CPU-only Iris job can call a pinned, allowed free model using a cluster-held credential, record results, and resume after restart without repeating completed examples.
- Shared request admission handles the free-tier minute/day limits, bounded retries, quota exhaustion, and upstream failures; clients cannot select paid models or access the upstream credential.
- With public prompts, run an initial pilot of up to eight examples per candidate, with at most 24 HTTP attempts total including retries. Report task success, tool/JSON validity where applicable, latency, rate-limit errors, returned model/provider, and reported cost. Retries reduce the number of distinct examples completed.
- Verify restart, quota exhaustion, and credential/model restrictions with tests; document any constraints discovered in the live Iris pilot.

No inference calls or Iris jobs have been run for this investigation.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖 # Research

The current Iris inference path is built around accelerator-backed model servers. Its worker forwards caller headers, and its broker keeps requests in memory; neither provides credential isolation, account-wide quota admission, or restart recovery for OpenRouter. The evaluation runner already submits a CPU orchestrator, but it resolves secret references before submission, so the proposed job must resolve its key inside the task. I found no open PR implementing OpenRouter support.

**Relevant code**
- [`config.py#L192`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/config.py#L192) — rejects CPU inference workers.
- [`worker.py#L125`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/worker.py#L125) — forwards caller headers upstream.
- [`broker.py#L67`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/broker.py#L67) — holds request state in memory.
- [`runner.py#L360`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L360) — CPU Iris submission pattern.
- [`secrets.py#L151`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/rigging/src/rigging/secrets.py#L151) — reference-based secret resolution.

# OpenRouter free-model pilot

Run a bounded manifest of public prompts through one CPU Iris coordinator. The first version should call OpenRouter directly from that task and write resumable results; it does not need to retrofit the accelerator-oriented proxy and worker. Existing endpoint-oriented evaluation work in [#4827](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/4827) remains useful for later evaluator integration.

## Challenges and costs

A free-model attempt can consume daily quota even if the client times out. A crash between upstream completion and result persistence leaves the outcome unknown, so restart recovery cannot promise exactly-once inference. The single coordinator also limits throughput; that fits the pilot's request cap. Existing clients using the same OpenRouter account can consume quota outside this job.

## Design and landing order

1. Add a typed manifest and CPU Iris submission entry in `marin/inference/` for pinned `:free` model IDs, prompt IDs, request parameters, a same-region output prefix, and explicit attempt and concurrency caps. Reject duplicate prompt IDs, model overrides, plugins, paid fallback models, and any ID outside a configured allowlist before the job starts. Check catalog pricing before dispatch and set a zero `provider.max_price` ceiling for prompt and completion tokens. Resolve a `rigging.secrets.SecretSpec` *inside* the coordinator from a cluster-projected environment/file secret or a versioned GCP Secret Manager reference; serialize only the reference into the job request. Keep the credential out of endpoint objects returned to callers and out of logs.
2. Give all jobs for this OpenRouter account one configured storage lock path, using the existing distributed lock, so only one coordinator admits requests at a time. At startup and after rate-limit errors, query `GET /api/v1/key` and require `free_model_daily_requests.remaining`. Admit at most 15 attempts per rolling minute and two concurrent calls, counting every retry and every reserved-but-uncertain attempt. Reserve each attempt durably before sending it; use the lower of the key endpoint's remaining count and the locally unspent daily budget. Pause at daily exhaustion and recheck after the UTC reset. Fail closed if the quota response or lock is unavailable.
3. Store one committed result per prompt ID and model, plus attempt records containing request ID, timestamp, requested and returned model, provider when reported, parameters, status, latency, usage, reported cost, and a redacted error. On restart, load committed results and attempt reservations, skip completed prompts, and put uncertain prompts back in the queue only if attempt and quota budgets allow. Honor `Retry-After`; retry 429, transient 5xx, and transport failures with bounded backoff. Stop on authentication, malformed configuration, or a response indicating a paid route. The prompt/result store should use existing `fsspec` and filesystem atomic-write helpers.
4. Add focused local tests with a fake HTTP server and temporary filesystem for restart, daily and minute exhaustion, 429 timing, timeout accounting, and credential/model restrictions. Then run a public-prompt Iris pilot of up to eight examples for each of the three candidates, with at most 24 total HTTP attempts including retries. Report successes, tool/JSON validity, latency, 429s, returned model/provider, cost, and any cluster or endpoint constraints. A timeout may cause a second upstream completion; the report must count both attempts.

## Open questions before the live pilot

- Which Iris cluster has approved outbound HTTPS, same-region result storage, and a task-visible secret source for the OpenRouter key? The current evaluation runner resolves secrets on the submitter, which does not meet this requirement.
- Does the account's actual `/api/v1/key` response enforce the free daily cap, and do the chosen models still advertise zero price and the required tool/JSON capabilities? Check both at pilot time; [OpenRouter's limits](https://openrouter.ai/docs/api_reference/limits) expose the daily counter, while the per-minute ceiling is not returned there.
- Are the selected models' data-retention and output-use terms acceptable for the intended evaluation inputs? Keep the pilot on public prompts until that is answered.

spillover_issues.body:
The SWE-smith Harbor task packages in `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s` (and the same layout in `mlfoundations-dev/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests`) leave the repository's full git history in the agent's container. The image built from `environment/Dockerfile` keeps a local `main` branch with the unbroken code and about 944 other branches, so the agent can print the fix with `git diff HEAD main -- <package>` or `git show main:<file>`. `/tests` and `/solution` are correctly absent from the image.

Reproduce: build `swesmith-00003`'s `environment/Dockerfile` from the package, run it with no network, then `git log --oneline` (three commits: Initial commit, Bug Patch, Remove F2P Tests), `git branch -a` (944 branches including `main`), `git diff HEAD main -- oauthlib` (the exact fix).

Impact on existing data: in `open-athena/Kimi-2.5-swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s-maxeps-32k`, 860 of 5,237 passing trials (16.4%) and 433 of 4,119 failing trials run history-reading commands (`git show main:<path>`, diffs against `main` or `HEAD~N`, checkout or restore from history, `git log -p`). Some are benign (a diff against `HEAD~1` shows only the removed tests); many copy the original file. So the reported pass rate on these packages is inflated, and trace sets built on them carry shortcut solutions: the Kimi set above, the `GLM-4.7` and AgentTrove swesmith streams, and the allkimi relay data (`laion/calibforge-relay-traces`, `kimi_swesmith` rows) that was DARE-grafted into Snowball v0 (`open-athena/Grug-67B-A2B-Merge-Campaign3-DARE-Linear-02-2026.10.12`). SWE-bench Verified is not affected: there the fix is not in the repository's past.

A plain squash is not enough, because `tests/test.sh` itself uses history (`git checkout <task branch>; git checkout HEAD~1`) to restore the removed fail-to-pass tests before running pytest.

Expected: during the agent phase the repository has one commit, no other branches, no remote and no reflog; the verifier restores the fail-to-pass tests from outside the agent's view (for example, ship the test files in `tests/` and copy them in, or keep a git bundle that only the verifier unpacks). For each task, the gold patch still passes, the unpatched repository still fails, and the history-reading commands above return nothing.

Done when: a fixed package build exists with that validation on a sample of tasks, existing SWE-smith pass rates and training sets built on the leaky packages are re-reported with history-reading trials removed or flagged, and the shootout pool in #10213 uses the fixed packages.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖

# Research

The reported `swesmith-00003` image retains the pre-bug `main` branch and earlier commits, so an agent can recover the fix from Git history. Removing old refs alone is insufficient if the object database still contains the clean tree; the current verifier also uses `HEAD~1` to recover fail-to-pass tests. The reported 860/5,237 passing and 433/4,119 failing history-reading trials are contamination candidates, not yet an audited count of trials that copied the fix. Marin consumes these external packages and traces, while the package builder is outside this checkout.

**Relevant code and artifacts**
- [DCAgent package release](https://huggingface.co/datasets/DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s) — affected task source.
- [Shootout #10213](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/issues/10213) — waits for stripped packages.
- [AgentTrove ingestion](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/44323775503ca44a2e8ef345bdcd45a6f0b5ba1e/lib/marin/src/marin/datakit/download/agenttrove.py#L17) — SWE-smith trace consumer.
- [Relay source PR #10027](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10027) — registers Kimi SWE-smith rows.

# Proposal

## Outcome

Publish an immutable, revision-pinned Harbor package release whose agent image contains the bugged working tree in one new Git repository with one commit, one task branch, no `main`/remote/tags/reflog, and no recoverable old objects. Keep the fail-to-pass test payload in Harbor's verifier-only `tests/` area and copy it into the repository when scoring. Record the old and new package revisions and per-task content digests; do not overwrite the release used by existing trials.

## Plan

1. Change the package producer to create a fresh `.git` after applying each bug patch, rather than squashing the existing repository in place. Export required test files from the source package into verifier-only storage before discarding history. Make `tests/test.sh` restore those files without `git checkout` or `HEAD~1`; keep `solution/` and `tests/` out of the agent container.
2. Validate a stratified sample across repositories and test layouts in offline Harbor runs. In each agent image, require one reachable commit and no old refs, remotes, reflogs, or dangling objects containing the clean fix. Exercise `git show main:<file>`, `git diff HEAD main -- <package>`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git log -p`, and `git fsck --unreachable`; none may reveal the clean file. For each sampled task, the untouched bugged tree must score 0 and the gold patch must score 1 under the revised verifier. Publish task IDs, package digests, commands, and results with the new release.
3. Audit the Kimi, GLM-4.7, AgentTrove, and allkimi relay/Snowball v0 provenance at trial or row level. Classify history commands as benign inspection, fix recovery, or unresolved; report raw and unflagged success rates with denominators, plus counts by outcome and category. Publish flagged row IDs or a reproducible manifest and clean-filtered trace revisions where the source can be republished. Annotate existing model and dataset results; filtering rows cannot undo training already performed on Snowball v0.
4. Pin the fixed package revision in the #10213 SWE-smith pool and block the eight-attempt generation until the package validation passes. Keep the already stated pilot-trace history filter separate from the new pool validation. Coordinate Harbor release acquisition with [#10198](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/pull/10198); its cache work does not repair the package contents.

## Risks and open questions

The package producer and release permissions are external to this repository, so the new dataset revision needs an owner with access to that build pipeline. The verifier payload must be checked against every sampled task's required test files; a one-commit image can still give false rewards if a file is omitted. Excluding all history-reading trials gives a conservative subset, not an unbiased replacement for a fresh evaluation on fixed packages.

comments.body:
🤖 Fixed SWE-smith packages for the #10213 pool, with validation on 20 tasks. The same class of leak is also present in TMax.

**Fixed packages.** `s3://marin-us-east-02a/marin/experiments/sft-shootout/pool/swesmith-packages.parquet` (sha256 `f004b109edf8aa9274693c07e01266d14469ec8c61fe695cc516aa1175117407`), 2,100 tasks. The schema is the same as the DCAgent parquet (`path`, `task_binary`), and the folder names are unchanged. The source is `DCAgent/swesmith-sandboxes-with_tests-oracle_verified_120s@78b0d879`. The upstream dataset is not modified. Code: [`experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool/`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/tree/3bc613878c/experiments/post_training/sft_shootout_pool) on branch `task/206`.

- `environment/Dockerfile`: after the upstream `git fetch && git checkout <instance>`, the same `RUN` replaces the repository: `rm -rf .git && git init && git symbolic-ref HEAD refs/heads/main && git add -A && git commit -m "Initial commit" && git reflog expire --expire=now --all && git gc --prune=now`. This is a new `.git`, not a squash, so no old objects remain in the container's filesystem. The base image's lower layers still hold the old `.git`, but the container cannot read them.
- `tests/f2p_restore/`: the files that the upstream `git checkout HEAD~1` would change, at their parent contents, plus `deleted.txt`. They are computed from a bare clone of `github.com/swesmith/<repo>`. On `swesmith-00003` they match the image's own `git show HEAD~1:<path>` byte for byte.
- `tests/test.sh`: `git checkout <instance>; git checkout HEAD~1;` is replaced by `cp -a /tests/f2p_restore/files/. /testbed/` plus the deletions. The rest is unchanged. Harbor uploads `tests/` only to the verifier (checked in harbor 0.24.0 `verifier/verifier.py`; only `agents/oracle.py` uploads `solution/`).

**Validation** on 20 pool tasks, one from each of 20 repos, in local Docker following Harbor's phase order:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Agent-phase repository: 1 commit, 1 branch, 0 remotes, empty reflog, no `HEAD~1`/`main~1`/`origin/main`/`master` | 20/20 |
| Gold patch (`solution/solve.sh`) then `tests/test.sh`: reward 1 | 20/20 |
| Unpatched tree: reward 0 | 19/20 |
| Leak commands (`git log --all -p`, `git show HEAD~1`, `git diff HEAD main`, `git diff HEAD~1`, `git fsck --unreachable --lost-found`, `git stash list -p`, `git show main:<every file>`) print a clean-only line | 0/20 (upstream `swesmith-00003` control: 2/2) |

- `swesmith-01094` (`ariga/atlas`) also scores 1 unpatched with the unmodified upstream package, so its verifier does not detect the bug. This is an upstream defect, and it means DCAgent's "oracle verified" does not imply that an unpatched run fails.
- "Clean-only line": a source line the Bug Patch removed that occurs nowhere in the bugged tree. 7 of the 20 tasks have none, so only the ref checks apply to them.
- The filesystem search found no git leak. It did find copies of clean lines in installed packages: `setuptools/_vendor/typeguard` is an older vendored typeguard, which is relevant for `agronholm/typeguard` tasks (57 in the pool). The `_pytest` (iniconfig) and `rapidfuzz` (thefuzz) hits are probably coincidental.
- Residual: `github.com/swesmith/<repo>` is public and keeps every instance branch, so an agent with internet access can still fetch the fix. In the Kimi traces this happened once (`git fetch origin; git show origin/main:<file>`).

Per-task results: `pool/swesmith-validation-20.jsonl` and `pool/swesmith-leak-probe-20.jsonl`.

**TMax: same class of leak, different mechanism.** In `allenai/TMax-SFT-16.5K@848e2182` `tasks.zip`, 221 of 2,200 environments build verifier assets into the agent's image (for example `/opt/oracle/<reference program>`, `/app/verifier/ground_truth_valid_events.txt`, `/home/user/oracle.py`), and `test_final_state.py` reads them. In 181 of the 221, the instruction never names the path. In the #202 Qwen3.6-27B success traces (`allenai/tmax-sft`), 63 trajectories across 18 tasks name one of these hidden paths in a bash command. That is a heuristic: naming a path doesn't prove the answer was copied. The pool excludes the 181 (`excluded.jsonl`, `leak_risk=hidden_verifier_assets`) and keeps the 40 visible ones. TMax's Harbor converter (`hamishivi/tmax@6d3d606c`) does not copy `task.json` (including its `truth` field), `solutions/`, `setup.sh` or `test_initial_state.py`; `test_final_state.py` goes only to `tests/`.

**Effect on #202's pilot training set:** 860 Kimi history-reading passes and those 63 TMax trajectories were removed before training (manifest `selection.swesmith_git_history_rule` and `selection.tmax_hidden_asset_rule`).

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
`remote_inference` resolves the served endpoint's address once (`lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py:682`) and keeps using it for the life of the client. When the inference task is preempted and Iris reschedules it on another host, every later request goes to the dead address and fails with `httpx.ConnectError: All connection attempts failed` until the client process restarts.

Observed on 2026-10-17 in the SFT-shootout relay collection (#10213): the v0 student server for TMax relay shard-02 round 1 (`inference-7998e252`) shows `preemptions=1` and its log stops at 14:35:18 UTC; from then on the relay proxy logged thousands of `ConnectError`s, 198 of 200 trials in that round raised `InternalServerError` between 14:33 and 15:13 UTC, and the driver still wrote `_SUCCESS` because Harbor exited 0. SWE-smith relay shard-00 round 3 failed the same way earlier that morning (85 of 97 trials raised; both student children of that job show `preemptions=1`).

Reproduce: serve a model through `remote_inference`, start a long-lived client, preempt (or cancel and let Iris reschedule) the inference task, send a request after the task is running again on a different host.

Expected: the client re-resolves the endpoint through Iris when a connection error occurs (bounded retry), so a rescheduled server is picked up without restarting the client; callers that cannot recover should fail loudly rather than report success.

Done when: `remote_inference` (or its client wrapper) re-resolves on connection failure with a bounded retry, a test covers a rescheduled endpoint, and callers that batch many requests (relay collection, eval launchers) surface a failed run instead of a success marker when the server is unreachable. The relay collector's own copy of this fix (re-resolve on `ConnectError`, retry up to 20 minutes, then fail the run when over 20% of trials raise) is on branch `task/212` at `174906474a` and can serve as a reference.

comments.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At main `2f3897eb`, direct `remote_inference` freezes the serving task's address. Evalchemy selects a direct route and resolves it once more before handing a fixed URL to lm-eval; its eight request retries cannot follow a rescheduled task. Harbor already uses the Iris capability route and a 90% completion gate, while an evaluation step can return successfully after writing a failed record. The relay collector's [address retry](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/174906474a8039d1ff8989e8f6d53103242cfec1) and [unserved-trial gate](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/commit/f547fdf339) are on `task/212`.

**Relevant code**
- [`iris.py#L656-L665`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f3897ebfdbdbc2246bbe0a3bf6bca91a89b6f9d/lib/marin/src/marin/inference/iris.py#L656-L665) — initial direct URL
- [`launch.py#L205-L236`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f3897ebfdbdbc2246bbe0a3bf6bca91a89b6f9d/experiments/evaluation/launch.py#L205-L236) — Evalchemy direct, Harbor capability
- [`runner.py#L556-L564`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f3897ebfdbdbc2246bbe0a3bf6bca91a89b6f9d/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L556-L564) — one-time direct resolution
- [`client.py#L143-L156`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f3897ebfdbdbc2246bbe0a3bf6bca91a89b6f9d/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/evalchemy/client.py#L143-L156) — fixed URL and eight retries
- [`runner.py#L460-L472`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/2f3897ebfdbdbc2246bbe0a3bf6bca91a89b6f9d/lib/marin/src/marin/evaluation/runner.py#L460-L472) — failed record returns as step success

# Proposed Fix

`remote_inference` → `_local_endpoint_session` → lm-eval retains the old URL after Iris moves the serving task. This needs changes at the session, evaluator route, and run-status boundaries:

1. Route Evalchemy model requests through the existing Iris capability URL, which resolves the current endpoint per request; retain the direct URL for metrics. Verify long-request timeouts and measure a representative evaluation's throughput before landing.
2. Add a session-owned direct endpoint resolver and use it in direct HTTP callers on `ConnectError`, with a monotonic deadline, bounded poll interval, and terminal-job check. Make `wait_until_ready()` probe the newly resolved address after rescheduling; propagate failure when the deadline expires.
3. After persisting a non-success evaluation record, raise from `run_evaluation_step` so the enclosing step cannot write a success marker. Reuse the existing Evalchemy/Harbor coverage checks and integrate the relay branch's unserved-trial gate without duplicating it.
4. Test a request across two local serving addresses, a permanently unavailable endpoint, Evalchemy's selected route, and failure propagation through the evaluation step. Run the touched package tests and repository lint before opening a PR.

spillover_issues.author: karansag
spillover_issues.body:
## tl;dr

* Iris would kill child jobs (e.g., a coordinator job that ran both training and evaluation; if the coordinator exits then the evaluation would get killed even if it's still running) even with PRESERVE_CHILD set. 
* Diagnostics for chained jobs was spotty
* Incorrectly accepted flags for federated jobs

## More Detail

Chaining training, export and evaluation through Iris exposes lifecycle and diagnostic problems: children can be killed after successful parent completion, in-task federation options can select the wrong submission route, endpoint readiness failures have inconsistent exception types, and hub status displays default limits for peer-created children.

Checked against main `7bd7e77fcfd7b7c5e7d8b8d18fcea9f4cd6839ec`.

Reproduce:
1. Submit a one-task or four-task parent with `PRESERVE_CHILDREN`, then a running child. Complete the parent's tasks successfully. The controller kills the child with `Parent job terminated`; `reconcile/batches.py` bypasses the policy for success.
2. Launch SkyRL from an Iris task while retaining `target_cluster` and `parent_cluster_config`. The launcher selects external federation submission rather than its ambient task client. A reported bare `ConnectError` obscured diagnosis; the exact historical RPC cause is not established.
3. Resolve an unregistered endpoint through the direct client. An empty registry raises builtin `ConnectionError`, while an RPC `NOT_FOUND` raises `ConnectError`. A readiness loop handling only one fails.
4. Create a child on a federation peer with nondefault timeouts/retry limits, then read its request from the hub. The mirror keeps default limits because federation sync omits them.

Done when:
- Successful parent completion honors the selected child-lifetime policy, with regression coverage for one-task and multi-task parents. Document the change to multi-task defaults and keep explicit cancellation behavior clear.
- Unsupported in-task federation routing fails early with actionable guidance, and submission failures expose RPC code and reason without losing structured details.
- Endpoint absence has one documented exception contract; readiness callers retry absence while preserving unrelated RPC failures.
- Hub mirrors report the peer's requested execution/scheduling timeouts and retry/failure limits, tested across the serialized federation boundary.
- `lib/iris/OPS.md` distinguishes child execution timeout from running CPU coordinator timeouts and application deadlines during Kueue admission waits.

Keep the fixes in draft PRs with focused tests. This work does not deploy controller changes or alter ongoing experiments.

comments.body:
🤖
# Research

At main `7bd7e77`, successful parent finalization cascades to children without checking the effective child policy; multi-task parents default to `PRESERVE_CHILDREN`. Direct endpoint lookup raises builtin `ConnectionError` for an empty registry, while RPC absence uses `ConnectError(NOT_FOUND)`. SkyRL clears federation fields when `get_job_info()` is present, so the reported external submission needs a launcher-level regression test; federation sync sends status but omits the limits needed for peer-created child mirrors. Searches found no open PR tied to #10768 or these root causes.

**Relevant code**
- [`batches.py#L164`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7bd7e77fcfd7b7c5e7d8b8d18fcea9f4cd6839ec/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/reconcile/batches.py#L164) — unconditional success cascade
- [`skyrl.py#L802`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7bd7e77fcfd7b7c5e7d8b8d18fcea9f4cd6839ec/lib/marin/src/marin/rl/skyrl.py#L802) — ambient route detection
- [`remote_client.py#L450`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7bd7e77fcfd7b7c5e7d8b8d18fcea9f4cd6839ec/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/client/remote_client.py#L450) — direct endpoint contract
- [`federation_service.py#L83`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7bd7e77fcfd7b7c5e7d8b8d18fcea9f4cd6839ec/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/federation_service.py#L83) — peer delta contents
- [`federation_store.py#L350`](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/7bd7e77fcfd7b7c5e7d8b8d18fcea9f4cd6839ec/lib/iris/src/iris/cluster/controller/federation_store.py#L350) — child mirror defaults

# Proposed Fix

1. Open a draft lifecycle PR. Gate the success cascade on the effective child policy. Test successful one-task and four-task parents with explicit preserve/terminate policies and the multi-task default; keep explicit cancellation covered. Update `lib/iris/OPS.md` to distinguish the running CPU coordinator timeout, child execution timeout, and application deadline while Kueue holds the child gang.
2. Open a draft SkyRL submission PR. Reproduce the in-task launch with both federation fields at the launcher boundary, reject unsupported routing before submission with guidance to use the ambient task client, and report the RPC code and reason while retaining the original structured `ConnectError` details.
3. Open a draft endpoint PR. Make an absent direct endpoint raise `ConnectError(Code.NOT_FOUND)`; make readiness loops retry that absence and known transient codes while propagating unrelated RPC errors. Cover empty-registry and RPC `NOT_FOUND` paths.
4. Open a draft federation mirror PR. Add the peer's requested execution/scheduling timeouts and retry/failure limits to the serialized job delta, populate them from peer job config, and write them to new child mirrors on full and incremental sync. Test the hub's readback after an actual serialized sync with nondefault limits.
